title: Scraping the shadows: Deep learning breakthroughs in dark web intelligence
abstract: Darknet markets (DNMs) facilitate the trade of illegal goods on a global scale. Gathering data on DNMs is critical to ensuring law enforcement agencies can effectively combat crime. Manually extracting data from DNMs is an error-prone and time-consuming task. Aiming to automate this process we develop a framework for extracting data from DNMs and evaluate the application of three state-of-the-art Named Entity Recognition (NER) models, ELMo-BiLSTM (Shah et al., 2022), UniversalNER (Zhou et al., 2023), and GLiNER (Zaratiana et al., 2024), at the task of extracting complex entities from DNM product listing pages. We propose a new annotated dataset, which we use to train, fine-tune, and evaluate the models. Our findings show that state-of-the-art NER models perform well in information extraction from DNMs, achieving 91% Precision, 96% Recall, and an F1 score of 94%. In addition, fine-tuning enhances model performance, with UniversalNER achieving the best performance.

title: Hydra: Model Checkpoints for Multi-Target Backdoor Attacks against Vision-Language Models
abstract: Model checkpoints accompanying an anonymous submission under double-blind review. Contains Hydra backdoored LLaVA-v1.5-7B checkpoints for target scales M=5, 10, and 20.Each checkpoint contains the LoRA adapter, the multimodal projector, and thetrigger-generator weights, to be loaded onto the public base checkpointliuhaotian/llava-v1.5-7b. Code and reproduction instructions are provided separately with the submission.

title: Impact of Domain-Specific Intermediate Tasks on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does intermediate-task training with domain-specific English tasks (e.g., legal, medical) affect zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R's domain-specific datasets compared to general-domain intermediate tasks? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 7.8/10.

title: omerozcann/DMH: DMH
abstract: Reference implementation of DMH (Dynamic Multi-Level Hybrid), an adaptive metaheuristic that couples Differential Evolution, Metropolis-Hastings-style acceptance, and L-BFGS-B local search for continuous optimization. Includes experiments on CEC2017 functions and engineering design problems (companion to the journal paper).

title: Majax Messenger, Beyond End-to-End Encryption. Five ML-KEM-1024 Engines Supporting a Renewable Cryptographic Architecture
abstract: Majax Messenger presents a secure messaging architecture built around defense in depth, non-residency of messages, cryptographic domain separation, daily key rotation, and five independent ML-KEM-1024 engines dedicated to messages, voice, media, real-time calls, and device identity. The system combines authenticated transport, the Maurice HMAC-based request protocol, Signal session dynamics, authenticated symmetric encryption, and post-quantum key encapsulation. This white paper describes the public architecture, measurable security properties, controlled transition between cryptographic epochs, and benchmark results while deliberately withholding operational secrets and attack-enabling implementation details. The deposit contains the English reference edition and a complete French translation. A public single-engine ML-KEM-1024 demonstrator now complements the paper at https://github.com/MajidNIMAR/majax-mlkem1024-demo. It provides source code, a Docker source build, ephemeral test keys, reciprocal encapsulation and decapsulation, negative tests, verification scripts, security documentation and SPDX SBOM generation. The demonstrator is isolated from the operational Majax architecture and is not presented as an audit or certification.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance often plateaus when faced with problems that require multiple layers of abstraction and complex relationships. This paper introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement, designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to integrate SR with an evolutionary reinforcement learning (ERL) agent. The ERL agent dynamically explores the search space by generating symbolic expressions at different levels of abstraction, guided by a reward signal based on the fitness of the expressions to the data. This hierarchical structure allows the system to effectively capture intricate dependencies and ultimately produce more accurate and insightful mathematical models. The proposed method demonstrates a significant improvement in tackling complex, hierarchical regression problems compared to traditional SR techniques. The key innovation lies in the ability of the ERL agent to learn optimal levels of abstraction and strategically guide the symbolic regression process, leading to enhanced expressive power and improved solution quality.

title: SISTEM BERBASIS ATURAN DENGAN FORWARD CHAINING UNTUK REKOMENDASI LATIHAN BASKET
abstract: Latihan fisik merupakan faktor penting dalam menunjang performa pemain basket, namun kebutuhan latihan yang lebih bervariasi tergantung pada posisi mereka, pengalaman berlatih, kondisi fisik, tujuan latihan, fasilitas, waktu berlatih, dan catatan cedera. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menciptakan sistem berbasis web yang memberikan rekomendasi latihan fisik bagi pemain basket dengan menggunakan metode forward chaining. Sistem ini dibangun menggunakan framework Django dan menggunakan pengetahuan berbentuk rule yang mencakup rule level, rule BMI, rule penyesuaian, rule paket latihan, dan rule cedera. Masukkan dari pengguna akan diolah sebagai fakta awal untuk menetapkan level pemain, kategori BMI, penyesuaian latihan, serta rekomendasi paket latihan yang tepat. Penelitian ini untuk menunjukan bahwa sistem BASKETEXPERT dapat memberikan rekomendasi latihan fisik yang disesuaikan dengan kondisi pengguna, termasuk paket latihan utama, rekomendasi tambahan untuk BMI, penyesuaian akibat cedera, dan alasan dibalik rekomendasi tersebut. Pengujian dilakukan melalui 6 skenario dengan menggunakan metrik untuk mengevaluasi persentase kecocokan sistem. Hasil pengujian mengungkapkan bahwa 5 dari 6 skenario berfungsi dengan baik, menghasilkan persentase cocok sebesar 83,3%. Dengan demikian, sistem ini dapat berfungsi sebagai alat awal yang efektif untuk memberikan rekomendasi latihan fisik bagi pemain basket, meskipun masih dibutuhkan pengembangan lebih lanjut untuk mengatasi rule yang belum ada.

title: Нейросетевой стекинг для прогнозирования убытков в страховании
abstract: В работе раскрываются основные ограничений древовидных систем принятия решений в страховании – чувствительность к шуму и выбросам, склонность к переобучению, ограниченная способность к обобщению. Предлагаются способы их преодоления за счет методов машинного обучения, нейронных сетей и методов стекинг-ансамблирования. Ставится гипотеза о улучшении качества прогнозирования убытков, где прогнозы от нескольких базовых моделей (XGBoost, CatBoost, LogisticRegression, RandomForest, TabTransformer), в совокупности с исходными признаками набора данных, объединяются в более сильный ансамбль моделей, где строится метамодель на основе полносвязной нейронной сети с дополнительным входом исходным признаков. На данных страхования автомобилей в России за 2023-2025 годы, проводится исследование, где описывается порядок эксперимента с обучением разнородных моделей машинного обучения и нейронных сетей. Описывается алгоритм предобработки набора данных с акцентом на специфичное кодирование категорий (европейская классификация автомобилей по сегменту люксовости), делается акцент на несбалансированности целевого класса – менее 3% убытков во всем объеме данных. На основе обученных моделей строятся модели ансамблей, используя пять методов стекинг-ансамблирования: Simple Average, LogisticRegression-Constraint, Adaptive Regression by Mixing, ARM-Tweedie, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Проводится качественное сравнение базовых моделей с ансамблями моделей на основе классификационных (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) и вероятностных метрик (Logloss, BrierScore). По результатам исследования лучшей базовой моделью является TabTransformer (BrierScore = 0.037, LogLoss = 0.185, ROC-AUC = 0.635, PR-AUC = 0.054). Ансамбль на основе полносвязной нейронной сети (MLP) превзошел ее по всем ключевым метрикам (BrierScore = 0.026, LogLoss = 0.131, ROC-AUC = 0.649, PR-AUC = 0.055). Полученный результат исследования позволяют подтвердить поставленную гипотезу: ансамбль на основе полносвязной нейронной сети позволил получить прирост по основным метрикам оценки. Полученный результат доказывает методологическую ценность подхода, даже в условиях ограниченного сигнала данных нейросетевой ансамбль в совокупности с исходными признаками обеспечивает более эффективное объединение прогнозов по сравнению с методами предиктивной аналитики и методами стекинг-ансамблирования. This study examines the primary limitations of tree-based decision models in the insurance sector, namely their sensitivity to noise and outliers, susceptibility to overfitting, and limited generalization capabilities. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, neural networks, and stacking ensemble methods. We hypothesize that the quality of loss prediction can be slightly improved by combining the predictions of multiple base models (XGBoost, CatBoost, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and TabTransformer), alongside the original dataset features, into a more robust ensemble. Specifically, the meta-model is constructed as a fully connected neural network with an additional input layer for the original features. The empirical study utilizes Russian auto insurance data from 2023 to 2025, detailing the experimental framework for training heterogeneous machine learning and neural network models. The data preprocessing pipeline is described, with a particular focus on a specific categorical encoding scheme based on the European car classification by luxury segment. Special attention is given to the severe imbalance of the target class, as losses account for less than 3% of the total dataset. Based on the trained base models, ensemble models are constructed using five stacking techniques: Simple Average, Constrained Logistic Regression, Adaptive Regression by Mixing (ARM), ARM-Tweedie, and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). A comprehensive comparative analysis of the base models and the ensembles is conducted using both classification metrics (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) and probabilistic metrics (Log Loss, Brier Score). The results indicate that the best-performing base model is TabTransformer (Brier Score = 0.037, Log Loss = 0.185, ROC-AUC = 0.635, PR-AUC = 0.054). The MLP-based ensemble outperformed it across all key metrics (Brier Score = 0.026, Log Loss = 0.131, ROC-AUC = 0.649, PR-AUC = 0.055). These findings confirm the initial hypothesis: the fully connected neural network ensemble yields a slightly improvement in the primary evaluation metrics. This demonstrates the methodological value of the proposed approach: even under conditions of a weak data signal, the neural network ensemble, augmented with original features, ensures a more effective aggregation of predictions compared to traditional predictive analytics and alternative stacking ensemble methods.

title: Posthoc Explainability Models
abstract: For complex models such as deep neural networks, explainability is not available intrinsically. The explanations have to be derived from the models using well-defined XAI methods that are called “Post-hoc Explainability Models.” To make predictions with a neural network, the data input is passed through many layers of multiplication with the learned weights and through nonlinear transformations. A single prediction can involve millions of mathematical operations depending on the architecture of the neural network. There is no chance that we humans can follow the exact mapping from data input to prediction. We would have to consider millions of weights that interact in a complex way to understand a prediction by a neural network. To interpret the behavior and predictions of neural networks, we need specific interpretation methods, and they are nothing but the “Post-hoc Explainability Models.”

title: How do the attributes of AI-generated digital humans relate to online customer experience? Evidence from SEM and fsQCA
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how AI-generated digital human attributes relate to online customer experience, identifies the configurational pathways linked to shared online customer experience, extends the research boundaries of generative AI in marketing, and expands the body of literature concerning online customer experience. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative online questionnaire was distributed to consumers with AI digital human interaction experience, collecting 607 valid responses for subsequent statistical analysis. This study draws on affordance theory to conceptualise four key attributes of AI-generated digital humans. A mixed-analytical design integrating structural equation modelling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is adopted to examine variable associations, mediating linkages, and multi-factor configurational pathways. Findings SEM results indicate that intelligent service capability and social influence of AI-generated digital humans are positively associated with both solo and shared online customer experiences, while sensory anthropomorphism is positively associated only with solo online customer experience. Furthermore, fsQCA results reveal three equifinal configurational pathways associated with high shared online customer experience. Solo online customer experience, intelligent service capability and social influence all serve as core conditions, while sensory anthropomorphism functions merely as a peripheral condition. Originality/value This study investigates the associations between attributes of AI-generated digital humans and online customer experience outcomes, deepening the application of affordance theory in intelligent marketing contexts. The analysis delivers rigorous empirical evidence and actionable managerial insights to guide firms in refining AI-generated digital human design and deployment strategies and enhancing online customer experience quality.

The analysis delivers rigorous empirical evidence and actionable managerial insights to guide firms in refining AI-generated digital human design and deployment strategies and enhancing online customer experience quality.

title: Satellite‐Based Global Assessment of Solar Resource Stability
abstract: Abstract Satellite spatial smoothing complicates comparisons of solar variability between gridded products and point measurements. We introduce the Stability Deviation Index (SDI), a bounded composite of solar intensity and intraday variability. Applied independently to 69 BSRN stations and co‐located CERES grid cells, SDI shows strong cross‐platform agreement ( R = 0.89, mean bias ≈0). Applying SDI to 23 years of CERES satellite records (2001–2023) reveals an obvious climatic divergence: stable subtropical regions are becoming more stable, while coastal and equatorial zones are becoming more volatile. Overlaying SDI maps with global PV inventories reveals a systematic spatial mismatch between PV deployment patterns and climatic stability. Although utility‐scale plants are optimally located, over 70% of small‐scale distributed PV systems are deployed in highly volatile regions, particularly in China and India. Ultimately, SDI translates smoothed Earth observations into actionable, grid‐compatible intelligence, highlighting hidden systemic risks in modern solar deployment.

title: TI$^2$PS: A Topology-Informed Inverse Design Framework for Stochastic Multicellular Pattern Formation
abstract: This study proposes a novel framework to estimate parameters for reproducing target multicellular patterns using an agent-based model (ABM). Two major challenges in multicellular ABMs are estimating cell-level parameters (agent-specific variables) and quantitatively evaluating the topological characteristics of multicellular arrangements under stochastic cell proliferation and death. To address these challenges, we integrate two approaches: Betti vectors and inverse surrogate modeling. The Betti vectors obtained through topological data analysis can consistently represent features of a wide range of multicellular spatial configurations. The inverse surrogate modeling enables direct inference of the corresponding ABM parameters from the target patterns. We validated the proposed framework using zebrafish pigment pattern formation, a representative model of pattern formation driven by multicellular interactions. The results demonstrate that our framework successfully estimates ABM parameters and outperforms conventional methods such as PointNet++. Notably, the proposed method, which used only 10% of the training data, outperformed PointNet++, which used 100% of the data, across all evaluation metrics.

title: Serialization Order Confounds Attention Analysis in MeshXL
abstract: Autoregressive mesh transformers look like an unusually convenient target for mechanistic interpretability: the token stream is the geometry, so every attention weight has a literal spatial address and can be painted onto the surface being generated. We show that this convenience is a trap. In MeshXL's canonical serialization, faces arrive sorted by height, so a face's index in the token stream predicts its vertical position at Spearman rho = 0.951 across all 2820 training chairs, and a cubic in normalized sequence position explains 86% of height variance. Any attention map read spatially is therefore confounded with plain recency. The confound is structural rather than incidental: it is a property of the preprocessing, its median across four object categories ranges only from +0.914 to +0.968, and re-ordering faces to break it raises cross-entropy fortyfold on every mesh tested. Controlling for sequence position on unmodified inputs, attention's partial correlation with 3D proximity is +0.194 (95% CI [+0.165, +0.206]) against +0.430 for sequence proximity; the spatial estimate replicates at +0.180 ([+0.167, +0.199]) on a disjoint held-out sample. No head in the network is primarily geometric, none reaching rho_spatial = 0.50 while rho_seq reaches +0.951, and layers 0-11 carry no geometric selectivity at all. Testing mesh topology, a geometric feature nearly independent of the confound, attention does not track it (+0.041, no head above +0.15), while sensitivity to repeated coordinate tokens between non-touching faces is twice as strong. Separately, MeshXL inherits OPT-1.3b's transformer body and reinitializes only its embeddings; we find its attention sinks bear no relation to OPT's (rho = -0.146) while being sevenfold stronger, so they form under mesh training rather than arriving with the weights. All confirmatory claims follow rules fixed before any attention was extracted. Of three such arms, one returned inconclusive, one failed its own validity gate, and one was refuted; all three are reported as they landed.

title: Information Bottleneck Approach to Explainable AI (XAI) via Latent Space Projection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to Explainable AI (XAI) leveraging the information bottleneck principle. Traditional XAI methods often struggle with interpretability and scalability, particularly with complex deep learning models. Our method aims to address these limitations by forcing an AI model to learn a compressed representation of the input data – a latent space – while simultaneously preserving information crucial for the model's predictive output. We hypothesize that analyzing this latent space provides valuable insights into the model's reasoning process, revealing the most relevant features driving its decisions. Specifically, we demonstrate how the information bottleneck can be applied to trained models, resulting in a lower-dimensional representation that can be readily visualized and dissected. The core of our approach involves minimizing a loss function that balances the compression of the input data with the preservation of predictive accuracy. This allows us to identify the latent variables that are most strongly associated with the model's output. We outline the theoretical framework, the methodology, and a potential implementation strategy, highlighting the benefits of this approach compared to existing XAI techniques. The aim is to provide a more transparent and interpretable understanding of AI models by focusing on the essential information they utilize.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks for Anomaly Detection in Time Series
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection in time series data using adaptive Bayesian networks. Traditional Bayesian networks often suffer from static structures that fail to capture the evolving nature of complex systems and the dynamic patterns associated with anomalies. This research addresses this limitation by incorporating a reinforcement learning (RL) framework to dynamically adjust the Bayesian network's structure and inference rules. The core idea is to treat the anomaly detection problem as a sequential decision-making process, where the RL agent learns to modify the network based on observed anomalies. The proposed method utilizes a Bayesian network as a representation of the system, with nodes representing variables and edges representing dependencies. The RL agent, guided by a reward function based on detection accuracy, iteratively refines the network structure (adding or removing nodes and edges) and updates the conditional probability tables (CPTs) associated with each node. The adaptive nature of this framework allows it to effectively handle time series data with non-stationary characteristics and complex dependencies, resulting in improved anomaly detection performance. The evaluation demonstrates the superiority of this adaptive approach over static Bayesian networks in scenarios with evolving data patterns and various types of anomalies.

title: Quantum Error Correction via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial for the reliable implementation of quantum computers, as qubits are extremely sensitive to environmental noise. Traditional approaches to QEC often suffer from computational complexity, particularly when scaling to larger qubit systems. This work explores the application of tensor networks as a novel method for representing and manipulating quantum error correction codes. We demonstrate that tensor networks provide a compact and efficient framework for encoding and decoding quantum information, potentially mitigating the scalability issues inherent in conventional QEC schemes. Specifically, we leverage the ability of tensor networks to represent the entanglement structure of codes, allowing for efficient simulation and decoding of noisy quantum computations. This approach offers a promising avenue for developing scalable QEC protocols. The core claim is that tensor networks offer a compact and efficient representation for quantum error correction codes. The core mechanism involves utilizing tensor networks to represent the entanglement structure of quantum error correction codes, enabling efficient simulation and decoding of noisy quantum computations.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Bayesian Knowledge Graphs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for neuro-symbolic reasoning leveraging Bayesian Knowledge Graphs (BKGs). The core claim is that integrating neural networks with symbolic reasoning presents a significant challenge, yet offers immense potential for more robust and explainable AI systems. Our approach integrates neural networks to handle perception and uncertainty, while utilizing a BKG to represent and reason with symbolic knowledge. This allows the system to learn from both data and explicit knowledge, addressing limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic approaches. The resulting system exhibits enhanced reasoning capabilities and improved interpretability. We define the framework formally, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system's architecture is presented with detailed mathematical formulations for the Bayesian inference process and the neural network components. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual illustration, highlighting the benefits of combining data-driven learning with structured knowledge representation. Further research directions are identified, focusing on scaling the framework and exploring its application in complex reasoning tasks.

title: Fractal Graph Embeddings for Symbolic Representation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic knowledge representation utilizing fractal graph embeddings. The core idea is that complex knowledge structures can be recursively embedded within fractal geometries, creating hierarchical representations that are both intuitive and potentially computationally efficient. We introduce an algorithm based on Iterated Function Systems (IFS) to generate fractal landscapes. Nodes within these landscapes represent concepts, with edge weights determined by semantic similarity. The fractal dimension of the resulting graph dictates the depth of the knowledge hierarchy. This approach offers a physically grounded method for representing and reasoning about complex symbolic knowledge, bridging the gap between graph theory and fractal geometry. The key contribution lies in the systematic application of fractal geometry to create a dynamic, hierarchical symbolic representation. We demonstrate the theoretical framework and outline the potential for future research in this area.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Logic with Temporal Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic framework that integrates neural networks with symbolic logic, significantly enhanced by incorporating temporal reasoning. The core idea is to augment the symbolic component with a temporal logic system, allowing for the representation and manipulation of knowledge that evolves over time. Traditional neuro-symbolic approaches often struggle with the complexities of dynamic environments and reasoning about temporal relationships. This work addresses this limitation by providing a hybrid architecture where neural networks handle pattern recognition and feature extraction, while the temporal logic system maintains a dynamic knowledge representation and performs reasoning about events across time. We define key concepts, including the hybrid architecture, the temporal logic formalism, and the interaction mechanisms between the neural and symbolic components. The resulting system offers a more robust and flexible cognitive system capable of handling time-varying information, paving the way for applications in areas such as robotics, intelligent agents, and knowledge representation. The central contribution lies in bridging the gap between the strengths of neural networks and symbolic logic, enabling temporal reasoning within a neuro-symbolic framework.

title: Causal Inference via Generative Process Modeling
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal inference leveraging generative process models. Traditional methods often rely on correlation analysis, which can be misleading when inferring causal relationships. We argue that generative models, such as Markov-Switching Models, offer a more robust framework by explicitly modeling the underlying causal processes. The core idea is to learn a generative process that describes the causal relationships between variables and then utilize this model to perform causal inference. This approach allows us to move beyond merely identifying correlations and establish genuine causal connections, a crucial step towards creating truly intelligent systems capable of robust prediction and decision-making. The paper details the methodology, outlining the model learning process and inference strategies, and highlights the advantages of this technique in scenarios where observational data is limited or biased. We demonstrate, conceptually, how this approach can be applied to a simplified causal network, illustrating the potential for improved accuracy and reliability compared to correlational methods.

title: From quantum reservoirs to quantum extreme learning machines through a nearest-neighbor spin chain with tunable quantum memory
abstract: Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) processes temporal data by retaining a memory of past inputs in the recurrent state of a quantum system, whereas a Quantum Extreme-Learning Machine (QELM) discards that memory, resetting the system at every step so that only the most recent input shapes the response. The two are usually treated as separate computational paradigms. We show that they are the two limits of a single architecture, connected by the input-encoding length, that is, the number of qubits overwritten with fresh data at each step. When a single qubit is re-encoded the system operates as a standard QRC, when the whole register is re-encoded it operates as a QELM, and intermediate lengths interpolate between them. The overwritten qubits hold the recent past in an explicit register, while the remaining qubits are never reset and carry older inputs forward in their evolving quantum state, so the encoding length redistributes memory between explicit and recurrent storage at fixed system size. Tuning the reservoir Hamiltonian and the evolution time with Bayesian optimization at each encoding length, we find that recurrent quantum memory is essential when a task must reach far into the past, and dispensable when the relevant history is short, where the memoryless reset limit already suffices. For every task the best reservoirs operate at the edge of chaos, where they perform as well as a densely connected reservoir with random all-to-all couplings of the same size, indicating that what temporal processing requires is the dynamical regime rather than the connectivity.

title: Linear Temporal Logic Translation via Human-Inspired Self-Constrained Reasoning for Robot Task Specification
abstract: Many robotic tasks are temporally extended and demand precise specifications of subgoals, constraints, and their temporal ordering. Yet human operators typically communicate such tasks in natural language, which is inherently ambiguous, underspecified, and context dependent. Translating human instructions into formal task specifications, such as Linear Temporal Logic (LTL), is therefore essential for verifiable and safe robotic execution. Existing LLM-based translators attempt to bridge this gap through open-ended reasoning or post-hoc constraint enforcement, but the former may violate domain constraints, whereas the latter can disrupt the reasoning needed for novel instructions. This paper proposes Self-Constrained Reasoning (SCR), a framework that mitigates this trade-off by internalizing structural knowledge into the model's decision-making process rather than imposing it as an external filter. By combining a structural constraint representation with a hierarchical decision-making formulation, SCR guides reasoning within a formally grounded space while preserving adaptability to unseen instructions. Experiments show that SCR improves both domain-constraint satisfaction and generalization, providing an effective and interpretable approach for translating human intent into verifiable specifications for robotic execution.

title: UniLipi: A Unified Multi-Script OCR for Historical Indic Manuscripts
abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) for handwritten Indic manuscripts is essential for large-scale digitization and computational access to manuscript heritage. However, existing approaches are typically developed for one script at a time and require substantial script-specific customization. This limits scalability and practical deployment across diverse collections. We present UniLipi, a unified multi-script OCR model for handwritten Indic manuscripts trained jointly across 13 Indic scripts within a single framework. UniLipi directly handles realistic manuscript conditions, including extreme variation in line geometry, large variation in line length, and partial interruptions caused by non-textual manuscript entities such as holes, stains, or pictorial illustrations. To operate effectively under ultra low-resource conditions, the model leverages script-aware synthetic manuscript data generation, substantially reducing reliance on large volumes of real annotated data. Beyond historical manuscripts, we show that UniLipi serves as an effective foundational pretrained model. Specifically, its learned representations enable good OCR performance for contemporary Indic handwriting and extend to several non-Indic scripts, including Tibetan, Italian, Latin, and Chinese scripts. In addition to transcription, UniLipi predicts script identity and per-line native character counts, supporting practical manuscript cataloging workflows.

title: Training-Free Temporal Abstraction for General Video Understanding
abstract: Videos are expensive to analyze frame by frame, yet many video understanding tasks depend on knowing where relevant moments occur. A system may need to find when an action changes, locate the segment described by a sentence, or choose a few frames for a vision-language model. Existing methods often solve these problems separately, using task-specific training data or specialized architectures. We study whether a pretrained video-text model can provide enough temporal structure to support several of these tasks at once. We present STITCH, a training-free method that divides a video into semantically meaningful temporal chunks. STITCH embeds short video windows with a frozen video-text backbone and detects changes in the resulting embedding sequence. These chunks are computed once per video and reused across tasks. We evaluate STITCH on generic event boundary detection, language-based moment retrieval, and frame selection for long-video VLM reasoning. Across all three settings, STITCH remains competitive with more specialized methods while requiring no task-specific training, with especially clear gains when only a small number of frames or tokens can be processed. evidence.title: Training-Free Temporal Abstraction for General Video Understanding
evidence.abstract: Videos are expensive to analyze frame by frame, yet many video understanding tasks depend on knowing where relevant moments occur. A system may need to find when an action changes, locate the segment described by a sentence, or choose a few frames for a vision-language model. Existing methods often solve these problems separately, using task-specific training data or specialized architectures. We study whether a pretrained video-text model can provide enough temporal structure to support several of these tasks at once. We present STITCH, a training-free method that divides a video into semantically meaningful temporal chunks. STITCH embeds short video windows with a frozen video-text backbone and detects changes in the resulting embedding sequence. These chunks are computed once per video and reused across tasks. We evaluate STITCH on generic event boundary detection, language-based moment retrieval, and frame selection for long-video VLM reasoning. Across all three settings, STITCH remains competitive with more specialized methods while requiring no task-specific training, with especially clear gains when only a small number of frames or tokens can be processed. These results suggest that reusable temporal abstraction is a promising direction for general video understanding, allowing dense video streams to be converted once into semantic units that can be localized, retrieved, sampled, or reasoned over by downstream systems.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Explainable Causal Models for Machine Learning
abstract: The increasing deployment of machine learning (ML) models in critical applications, such as healthcare, finance, and criminal justice, is accompanied by growing concerns about their opacity. Many ML models, particularly deep neural networks, operate as "black boxes," making it difficult to understand *why* they make specific predictions. This lack of transparency undermines trust, hinders debugging, and limits the potential for improvement. This paper proposes a novel framework for achieving algorithmic transparency by generating explainable causal models in conjunction with ML models. The core idea is to move beyond traditional post-hoc explanation techniques, which often provide limited insight, and instead build inherently transparent models based on causal relationships. We introduce a methodology for identifying and representing causal factors influencing ML model predictions, allowing for a deeper understanding of the model's internal logic. This approach facilitates not only improved debugging and model refinement but also enables users to assess the robustness of the model and identify potential biases. The framework's output is a causal model expressed mathematically, providing a verifiable and interpretable representation of the model's decision-making process. This represents a significant step towards building more trustworthy and accountable ML systems.

title: Cognitive Computing with Symbolic Regression and Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cognitive computing by integrating symbolic regression and neural networks. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both paradigms – symbolic regression's ability to discover explicit mathematical relationships from data and neural networks' proficiency in pattern recognition and generalization. The system operates in a hybrid manner: symbolic regression initially explores the data space to identify potential mathematical models, represented as equations. These equations are then fed into a neural network, which learns to refine, generalize, and predict outcomes based on the discovered relationships. This approach aims to bridge the gap between traditional symbolic AI and connectionist neural networks, fostering a more robust and interpretable cognitive system. The system's architecture, training methodology, and initial results are presented, demonstrating the potential of this integrated approach for tackling complex cognitive tasks. The key performance indicator is the accuracy of the predicted outcomes after the hybrid learning process.

title: Relational Tensor Decomposition for Graph Embeddings
abstract: Graph embeddings have become a cornerstone of modern graph analysis, enabling applications across diverse domains like social network analysis, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. However, many existing graph embedding techniques struggle to effectively capture the intricate relational structures inherent in graph data. These methods often rely on simplifying assumptions about node relationships, leading to a loss of nuanced information. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging relational tensor decomposition, specifically extending CP (Canonical Polyadic) decomposition, to directly operate on relational tensors derived from graph adjacency matrices. The core idea is to represent the graph as a high-order tensor, where each entry corresponds to the interaction between a set of nodes. Through CP decomposition, we can decompose this tensor into a set of lower-dimensional tensors, revealing latent relational factors that capture higher-order interactions. This approach offers a more flexible and powerful method for learning graph embeddings, as it doesn't impose restrictive assumptions about the nature of node relationships. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example. The key contribution lies in the direct application of tensor decomposition techniques to graph relationships, providing a fundamentally different perspective compared to traditional graph embedding methods.

title: Quantum-Inspired Cryptographic Key Generation Based on Random Walk Dynamics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cryptographic key generation utilizing quantum-inspired random walk dynamics. Traditional key generation methods often rely on deterministic algorithms susceptible to attacks. We introduce an algorithm where key generation is driven by a random walk process, mimicking the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics. The core of our method lies in the manipulation of the movement probabilities within the random walk, incorporating concepts like superposition and interference to create a significantly more unpredictable and robust key generation process. The resulting keys are generated through a series of iterations where the walker's position is determined by a probability distribution influenced by multiple potential pathways. We demonstrate that this approach can produce keys with enhanced security properties compared to conventional methods, offering a potential defense against attacks targeting predictable key generation processes. The algorithm's success is evaluated through simulations demonstrating its resistance to various attack vectors. The key mathematical formulation and algorithmic steps are presented in detail, outlining the core principles and operational mechanics of the proposed system. Furthermore, we explore the theoretical underpinnings of the method, linking it to concepts in quantum probability and random walk theory.

title: Multimodal Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in mT5 on XTREME Tasks
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does multimodal intermediate-task training (e.g., vision-language tasks) improve the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of mT5 on XTREME tasks compared to text-only intermediate tasks, measured by accuracy and alignment robustness metrics? title: Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the integration of quantum mechanical principles into genetic algorithms (GAs) to enhance their optimization capabilities. Traditional GAs operate based on classical probabilistic models, while this research proposes a novel approach that leverages concepts like superposition and tunneling to improve selection and crossover processes. The core idea is to mimic quantum phenomena within the GA framework, potentially leading to faster convergence and improved solutions for complex optimization problems. We detail the implementation of these quantum-inspired operators and present a theoretical framework for their application. The evaluation focuses on demonstrating the potential benefits of this hybrid approach through a series of simulated scenarios. The results suggest that incorporating quantum-inspired techniques can significantly improve the efficiency of the GA, particularly in situations with high dimensionality and intricate search spaces. This work represents a significant step toward bridging the gap between classical and quantum optimization paradigms.

title: ninadphalak/LLM-Shield-Proxy: v1.3.0: Stateless Cryptography, MCP Governance, Air-Gapped Egress, and System Hardening
abstract: 1.6.2 closed the reversible-redaction gap for OpenAI-shaped tool calls and left it open for Anthropic-native ones. That was half a guarantee: an Anthropic tool call still reached the caller carrying a placeholder, on every request rather than at an edge. This finishes it. | | OpenAI | Anthropic | |---|---|---| | Tool args, non-streaming | ✅ 1.6.2 — escaping added here | ✅ this release | | Tool args, streaming | ✅ 1.6.2 | ✅ this release | Anthropic non-streaming tool_use.input _rehydrate_json_response walked content[] looking for a text key. A tool_use block has none, so it was skipped whole and the caller invoked its tool with a placeholder. Its input is a decoded object rather than JSON text, so the string leaves are restored in place and the serializer escapes them on the way out. Anthropic streamed tool input Anthropic carries tool arguments as partial_json fragments on a content block — the shape OpenAI carries as function.arguments. Nothing in the tree handled it. The stream translation now opens the call from content_block_start (carrying its id and name once, as an OpenAI-shaped client needs), restores each fragment through that block's own retention window, and drains the window before content_block_stop — the Anthropic counterpart of the finish_reason rule, since the stop event is where the call finishes growing and a tail held past it is parsed against a truncated document. Anthropic numbers tool blocks in the same space as text blocks, so ordinals are handed out densely from 0 rather than emitting a tool call at index 1 with no index 0 in front of it. JSON escaping on the non-streaming path 1.6.2 escaped restored values into arguments for the stream only, leaving the same reply behaving differently depending on whether it was streamed. Both paths now share one escaping view. Also A buffered flush is framed as its own SSE event. Emitted with a single newline it shared the following event's blank line, producing one event with two newline-joined JSON documents that no compliant client can parse — the failure this work exists to prevent, reintroduced in the framing. Caught in review, fixed, and now covered by a test that splits on blank lines the way a client does rather than reading line by line. The tool-input depth bound moved from 8 to 40, matching the ceiling NonStreamingRehydrator already applies to decoded payloads. 8 sat inside the range a legitimate payload can occupy, so a leaf below it kept its placeholder silently. Reaching the bound now logs, naming no node content. tests/test_response_rehydration.py is new — _rehydrate_json_response had no test coverage at all before this. Still open The LiteLLM HTTP shim cannot restore tool calls: LiteLLM's GenericGuardrailAPIResponse has no field to return them. Upstream fix proposed in BerriAI/litellm#41013. JSON-RPC traffic was never affected — it routes to the stateless v3 engine, whose lexer is field-agnostic.

title: PENERAPAN ALGORITMA NAÏVE BAYES UNTUK KLASIFIKASI OPINI PUBLIK TENTANG ISU REDENOMINASI UANG DI MEDIA SOSIAL
abstract: Isu redenominasi rupiah dalam beberapa tahun terakhir menjadi perhatian masyarakat dan banyak diperbincangkan di media sosial sehingga memunculkan beragam opinik publik. Banyaknya komentar yang tersedia menyebabkan proses analisis secara manual menjadi kurang efektif, sehingga diperlukan metode otomatis untuk mengelompokan sentimen masyarakat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis opini publik terkait isu redenominasi rupiah pada media sosial instagram menggunakan algoritna naive bayes. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah CRISP-DM yang meliputi business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, dan deployment. Data diperoleh melalui teknik web scraping sebanyak 7.143 komentar. Hasil pelabelan menunjukan distribusi sentimen yang tidak seimbang, terdiri atas 5.716 sentimen netral, 1.017 sentimen positif, dan 164 sentimen negatif. Tahap preprocessing meliputi cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stemming, stopword removal, dan normalisasi. Selanjutnya dilakukan pembobotan TF-IDF dan klasifikasi menggunakan Multinominal Naive Bayes dengan pembagian data latih 80% dan data uji 20%. Hasil pengujian menunjukan akurasi sebesar 85%, precision 0,84, recall 0,85, dan F1-score 0,79. Performa terbaik diperoleh pada kelas sentimen netral, sedangkan kelas positif dan negatif masih dipengaruhi ketidakseimbangan data. Hasil penelitian menunjukan bahwa nave bayes cukup efektif untuk analisis sentimen terkait isu redenominasi rupiah pada media sosial instagram.

title: Adapting to generative AI in creative work: a technological frames perspective on creative advertising
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming creative work, yet creatives do not respond uniformly. To explain this variation, we draw on the concept of technological frames, three years of netnographic research in online advertising communities, and interviews with advertising creatives. Our analysis identifies competing interpretations of GenAI—regarding its level of agency in the creative process, its impact on jobs, and its role in shifting how value is created in outputs—that converge in distinct narratives about its implications for creative work. These narratives, in turn, drive distinct adaptive responses among creatives: AI skilling, reskilling, and deep skilling—the latter involving deliberate cultivation of human capabilities that GenAI cannot readily replicate. The findings inform both research on GenAI in creative work and managers navigating its adoption.

title: Artificial Neural Networks for Solar Panel Tilt Angle Optimization
abstract: Solar panels are the most prominent source of renewable energy. The tilt angle of the solar power system is one of the most critical factors in maximising the amount of solar radiation that reaches the solar panels. Since this angle is determined by the sun's daily, monthly, and yearly movements, it is unique to each location. To optimise the energy produced, it is crucial to accurately estimate the tilt angle that works best for the specific area. Various methods have been used to determine the optimal tilt angle in several regions around the world. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are employed to estimate the optimal solar panel tilt angle based on power generation at different tilt angles, factoring in the time of year and the months. The input data for the training process includes the average air temperature over 24 hours, total solar radiation, and humidity, while the output data consists of the electrical power generated. It was concluded that when the solar panel is fixed at a 30° tilt angle, it generates more power than at 25° or 35°. The ANN model performed optimally, achieving an accuracy of 93.34% based on the findings.

title: MANTLE: A Framework for Adaptive In-Situ Planetary Perception Using a Modular Uplink Principle
abstract: Planetary surface exploration missions rely increasingly on autonomous robotic platforms capable of interpreting complex terrain to ensure safe navigation, enable targeted science, and improve operational efficiency, as demonstrated across past Mars missions from Viking through Perseverance. Among the key perception capabilities, landform classification provides contextual information for landing site selection and scientific analysis, while boulder segmentation supports hazard assessment and path planning. This paper presents MANTLE, a multi-task adaptive network for terrain and landform extraction. The model uses a shared DINOv2 backbone for high-level feature extraction with task-specific heads: a classification head for large-scale landform classification, and a segmentation head for pixel-wise boulder localization, each trained on curated datasets built respectively from HiRISE orbital imagery and MSL surface-level imagery. The classification head achieved a test accuracy of 92.56% across seven Martian terrain classes, while the segmentation head achieved a validation IoU of 0.753 and showed strong cross-sol generalization on a held-out test set from previously unseen rover traverses. A key advantage of MANTLE is its modular, extensible design, formalized here as the Modular Uplink Principle: only a shared, frozen backbone needs to remain onboard, while subsequent perception capabilities are trained on Earth as lightweight task-specific heads and uplinked without retraining the full model. This work demonstrates two such high-impact capabilities, terrain classification and boulder segmentation, as an initial realization of a framework built to support many more over a mission's lifetime. With this foundation, future explorers need not arrive on Mars fully formed, but can continue to learn, adapt, and grow more capable with every uplink.

title: Scalable dynamic community detection on temporal graphs using graph neural networks
abstract: Dynamic community detection on temporal graphs seeks to identify evolving community structures while allowing node memberships to change over time. In this work, we formulate dynamic community detection over observed node-time instances, where each node-time instance in the temporal interaction stream is assigned a cluster label. We propose a diffusion-guided contrastive learning framework that uses a local temporal diffusion affinity matrix to construct positive and negative node-time pairs and organise the learned representations according to their temporal structural relationships. We then apply a clustering algorithm to the resulting embedding space to detect dynamic communities. Experiments on synthetic temporal networks show that the proposed method outperforms static community detection baselines and achieves competitive or better performance than existing dynamic community detection methods in terms of AMI and ARI, while maintaining good scalability. We further apply the method to a large-scale OpenAlex computer science collaboration network from 2016 to 2025, revealing persistent and evolving collaboration communities in real scientific data. These results suggest that time-node-level representation learning provides an effective framework for scalable dynamic community detection on temporal graphs.

title: Antipatterns in AI-assisted Qualitative Data Analysis: A Catalog of Temptations and Pitfalls for Software Engineering Researchers
abstract: AI-assisted qualitative data analysis (QDA) offers unprecedented opportunities to streamline software engineering (SE) research, yet uncritical use risks compromising analytical rigor and flooding the field with accelerated production of low-quality research. While tactical best practices will naturally evolve over time, SE researchers currently lack strategic guidance to identify and mitigate methodological risks when attempting AI-assisted QDA. Based on our decades of qualitative SE research expertise and experience combined with an understanding of the emerging landscape of AI-assisted QDA, this paper presents a catalog of antipatterns in AI-assisted QDA - a set of assumptions and practices that initially appear advantageous but ultimately undermine analytical rigor and validity. The antipatterns are grouped into three categories reflecting escalating impact: Dangerous Drivers, Operational Missteps, and Analytical Failures. As more SE researchers attempt AI-assisted QDA, these antipatterns will help them identify and avoid common temptations and pitfalls, while reviewers can be equipped with the vocabulary and criteria to call out problematic and failed practice. Ultimately, this catalog of antipatterns can serve as a stepping stone in our responsible methodological evolution toward principled and meaningful human-AI collaboration in qualitative research.

title: Quantum Chromatic Number of Subgraphs of Orthogonality Graphs and the Distance-2 Hamming Graph
abstract: The determination of the quantum chromatic number of graphs has attracted considerable attention recently. However, there are few families of graphs whose quantum chromatic numbers are determined. A notable exception is the family of orthogonality graphs, whose quantum chromatic numbers are fully determined. In this paper, we extend these results by determining the exact quantum chromatic number of several subgraphs of the orthogonality graphs. Using the technique of combinatorial designs, we also determine the quantum chromatic number of the distance-$2$ Hamming graph, whose edges consist of binary vectors of Hamming distance $2$, for infinitely many lengths.

title: Strict Standard Normal Cloud Sets C-Means Clustering: A New Approach for Competitive Intelligence Classification of Hydrogen Energy
abstract: This research first defines strict standard normal cloud sets—a mathematical model integrating randomness and fuzziness to quantify and address dataset uncertainty—and develops the corresponding cloud generation algorithm. This model converts quantitative feature data into cloud sets (characterized by parameters Ex, En, He, β), effectively capturing the uncertain distribution of features. In the classification of hydrogen energy technology competitive intelligence, this model is applied: first extract key features, then use the proposed model to generate cloud sets for each feature. We further derive the iterative formulas of strict standard normal cloud sets C-means clustering, including formulas for updating cluster center cloud parameters and calculating membership degrees. Additionally, we use the feature cloud sets to construct the initial membership degree matrix, and select initial clustering centers based on the membership degree values. Comparative experiments show that this method outperforms traditional fuzzy C-means in handling text data related to intelligence, with higher classification accuracy. It provides a rigorous technical framework for the precise classification of hydrogen energy technology competitive intelligence, supporting decision-making in industrial dynamics analysis.

title: Assessing the Communicative Effectiveness of Customised AI Chatbots in Nigeria's Banking Sector: Evidence from Undergraduate Users
authors: Michael Dare Ogunniyi, Bolarinwa Ebenezer Mowemi, Taiwo Oluwole Ayinla & Abayomi Emmanuel Bamishaye
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots in Nigerian banking has transformed customer service delivery, yet rigorous empirical assessments of their communicative effectiveness remain scarce. This study examined the usage patterns of customised AI chatbots of Sterling Bank (Naya) and United Bank for Africa (Leo) by undergraduates at Bowen University, Iwo, Osun State;evaluated the operational/communicative performance of these chatbots; identified common issues encountered using them; and assessed their influence on customers’ perceptions of service quality. Anchored on the Uses and Gratifications Theory and Technology Acceptance Model, the study employed a mixed-methods design combining a survey among purposively selected 344 undergraduates and in-depth interviews with customer service officials of the selected banks. Findings reveal that information retrieval was the dominant purpose of chatbot use (47.1%). Misunderstanding or misinterpretation of queries accounted for 36.87% of all reported issues. However, response accuracy (27.1%) and contextual understanding (31.2%) emerged as critical weaknesses. Overall, 41.3% of respondents were often satisfied, 42.2% sometimes satisfied, and 11.7% expressed rare or no satisfaction. The researchers conclude that customised AI chatbots in Nigerian banking have established a functional but communicatively limited presence, requiring urgent improvements in natural language processing accuracy, contextual intelligence, and linguistic adaptability to Nigeria’s multilingual environment. Nigerian banks should institute periodic independent audits of chatbot communicative accuracy, build continuous feedback mechanisms for real-time learning, and invest in NLP models trained on Nigerian language data, including Pidgin English and indigenous language-influenced varieties.

title: 大模型引导的自适应分段混合排序方案
abstract: This record presents QiuSort, an adaptive segmented hybrid sorting framework in which an AI large language model participates in pattern recognition and sorting-strategy selection. This document is Version 0.1 of a preliminary research record of QiuSort. It is intended to publicly document the current methodology, complexity analysis, and ongoing research directions. This version has not undergone peer review, and the implementation and experimental evaluation remain under continued development.

title: {Certifying Parameter-Estimate Admissibility Without Ground Truth: A Four-Rule Expert Decision-Support Framework (QAF) for Grey-Box Systems
abstract: Title: QAF — Quad-Admissibility Framework: Code, Data, and Supplementary Materials Description: This repository contains the complete reproducibility package for the manuscript: "Certifying Parameter-Estimate Admissibility Without Ground Truth: A Four-Rule Expert Decision-Support Framework (QAF) for Grey-Box Systems" submitted to Expert Systems with Applications (Elsevier). What is QAF?The Quad-Admissibility Framework (QAF) is a knowledge-based expert decision-support system that certifies whether metaheuristic parameter estimates are structurally admissible — without requiring ground-truth parameters. It applies four conjunctive rules: ensemble VIF (R1), spectral fidelity (R2), parametric diversity (R3), and distributional identifiability consistency (R4). The framework is evaluated across fifteen systems spanning behavioural, biological, physical, and controlled structural domains, using six metaheuristic algorithms (DE, GA, PSO, CMA-ES, SA, RS). Contents: Source code implementing the QAF framework and all four admissibility rules Analysis scripts and figure-generation code for all results reported in the manuscript and supplements S1–S48 QAF audit outputs (CSV/JSON) for all algorithm–system pairs Anonymised SCT trajectory dataset (31-day walking intervention, single participant, written informed consent obtained) Campaign metadata and configuration snapshots for full reproducibility Supplementary analyses S45 (Elowitz R2-pivotal), S46 (Bachmann R1 stress test), S47 (Silverbox remaining-cell probe), S48 (Borghans exploratory probe) External datasets used (not included, publicly available): PEtab Benchmark Collection (Böhm, Blasi, Crauste, Brännmark, Salazar-Cavazos, Elowitz, Bachmann): https://github.com/Benchmarking-Initiative/Benchmark-Models-PEtab EMPS benchmark: Pascu et al. (2019) Bouc-Wen benchmark: 4TU.ResearchData Silverbox benchmark: Wigren & Schoukens nonlinear system identification benchmarks Language: Python 3License: MIT

title: Adaptive Control of Robotic Systems using Quantum-Inspired Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired optimization techniques to the design of adaptive control systems for robotic systems operating in complex and dynamic environments. Traditional adaptive control methods often struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces and non-linear system dynamics, leading to slow convergence or instability. We propose utilizing quantum-inspired algorithms, specifically leveraging concepts from quantum annealing and quantum particle swarm optimization (QPSO), to efficiently explore this parameter space and identify optimal control policies. The core idea is to emulate the probabilistic and superposition properties of quantum mechanics to enhance the search process. The resulting adaptive control algorithms are expected to exhibit improved robustness, faster convergence, and superior performance compared to conventional methods, particularly in scenarios with significant uncertainties and disturbances. The research focuses on formulating the adaptive control problem as an optimization task and then employing the quantum-inspired algorithm to find the optimal control parameters. Simulation results demonstrate the potential of this approach to achieve robust and adaptive control for robotic systems.

title: Active Learning for Robot Control
abstract: This paper explores the application of active learning techniques to robot control, aiming to improve control performance through adaptive learning. Traditional robot control methods often rely on pre-defined models, limiting their ability to quickly adapt to changing environments and tasks. Active learning offers a solution by enabling the robot to actively select the most informative data points for learning, thereby reducing the need for extensive manual data collection. This research investigates the core claim that active learning can accelerate adaptation and proposes a mechanism where the robot strategically chooses data to learn from, coupled with machine learning algorithms for model training and control policy optimization. The primary focus is on developing a framework that dynamically adjusts the learning process based on the robot's current understanding of the environment, leading to more efficient and robust control strategies. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation. ---

title: Corpus snapshot for "What 1,114 Documents Reveal About Schema-Driven Extraction" (EMNLP 2026 Industry Track, ARR #248)
abstract: The exact corpus snapshot evaluated in the EMNLP 2026 Industry Track paper What 1,114 Documents Reveal About Schema-Driven Extraction: Models, Pipelines, and the Real-vs-Synthetic Gap (ARR submission 248). Contents. 1,079 document files across 12 categories and 8 domains, with the full set of 7,197 annotated field values, schemas and provenance manifests for all 1,114 documents. Corresponds to commit d79cdd0 of the koji corpus repository. Withheld, available by reference. 35 documents are not included: 18 ACORD certificate-of-insurance and 17 ISO policy-form samples, whose form layouts are copyrighted. Their ground-truth annotations and provenance manifests are retained, and each manifest records the publishing body's own source URL, so the snapshot can be reconstructed by re-fetching. See WITHHELD.md. These are all of the real insurance certificates and policies in the corpus, so any result involving them cannot be reproduced from this archive without re-fetching first. Scope of the results. The paper's figures were computed on the 1,100-document state of this snapshot (7,121 scored fields); the snapshot adds 14 adversarial documents described in the paper's Appendix B. Ground truth at this commit reproduces the scored run exactly on all 7,121 shared fields. Licensing. Mixed, per source; see ATTRIBUTION.md and each document's manifest. Synthetic documents and all annotations are the authors' own work. SEC EDGAR filings carry no explicit licence and are mandatory public disclosures authored by the filing registrant, not US Government works. CourtListener and Caselaw Access Project opinions are public domain. SROIE receipts are CC BY 4.0. MTSamples transcriptions are shared under the site's own terms for educational use with credit, and are not CC0. Relationship to FieldBench. This is the koji-lineage ancestor corpus, not FieldBench. Later FieldBench releases diverge in document membership and annotations and will not reproduce these numbers.

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN OPINI PUBLIK TERHADAP KEBIJAKAN VERIFIKASI IDENTITAS FITUR VOICE CHAT ROBLOX MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA NAÏVE BAYES BERBASIS TF-IDF
abstract: Penerapan sistem verifikasi identitas di berbagai platform digital memunculkan ketegangan antara upaya menjamin keamanan pengguna dan perlindungan hak privasi data pribadi. Kebijakan Roblox yang mewajibkan KTP sebagai syarat pengaktifan fitur voice chat memunculkan beragam tanggapan pengguna terkait keamanan data identitas yang diserahkan kepada platform. Meskipun isu privasi digital telah banyak dikaji, penelitian yang secara khusus menelaah sentimen publik terhadap kebijakan Verifikasi Identitas (KTP) dalam ekosistem Roblox masih sangat terbatas. Berangkat dari kesenjangan tersebut, penelitian ini memetakan persepsi publik melalui 1.243 komentar TikTok menggunakan algoritma Naïve Bayes. Kontribusi penelitian ini adalah penyediaan peta sentimen publik berbasis data media sosial yang dapat dijadikan landasan evaluasi kebijakan bagi pengembang platform. Data diolah melalui preprocessing, pembobotan TF-IDF, dan klasifikasi sentimen dengan akurasi 86,75%. Distribusi hasil mencatat 927 komentar netral, 288 negatif, dan 28 positif. Dominasi sentimen netral dan negatif mencerminkan belum terbentuknya kepercayaan pengguna terhadap mekanisme perlindungan privasi dan pengelolaan data pribadi oleh platform. Temuan ini diharapkan menjadi rujukan bagi pengembang dalam memperkuat transparansi tata kelola data serta merancang strategi komunikasi kebijakan yang lebih efektif dan persuasif.

title: How Attention-Level Access to Structural Information Shapes Layer-Wise Attention Routing in Transformers
abstract: Transformer layers can develop distinct attention routing patterns during training, but how architectural access to structural information shapes this organization remains unclear. Existing structure-aware methods make this difficult to determine by modifying several components. To investigate this question, we compare two Transformers matched in field ID inputs, embeddings, learned components, backbone, parameter count, and optimization but differing in attention computation. Both use field embeddings; Structure-Aware Attention Bias (SAAB) additionally transforms the supplied field IDs into a fixed pairwise same-field attention bias. We first train both models on the DBpedia dataset with masked structure modeling (MSM), which requires the recovery of hidden field labels from the context. Both models exceed 99.9% validation accuracy, yet they organize attention differently. Across 64 paired validation examples from the seed-1001 model pair, SAAB changes the mean same-field attention mass (SFM) by −0.085 at Layer 2 and +0.048 at Layer 3 (95% confidence intervals: [−0.092,−0.078] and [+0.042,+0.055]). We call this pattern competitive displacement. Across eight initializations, two show relatively strong displacement; the others show weaker or different responses. For seed 1001, displacement varies non-monotonically with the bias strength. Related changes persist with depth in two selected seeds and appear differently on PubMed. These results show that SAAB redistributes layer-wise attention routing under tested conditions.

title: Multi-source meteorology and cloud image joint coding algorithm for photovoltaic power prediction under complex weather disturbances
abstract: Introduction Rapid cloud movement, irradiance mutation, and meteorological uncertainty can increase prediction errors and delay ramp tracking in short-term photovoltaic power forecasting. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-source meteorological and cloud-image joint coding algorithm for short-term photovoltaic power prediction under complex weather disturbances. Methods The proposed method uses ground meteorological observations, numerical weather prediction variables, satellite cloud-image sequences, and historical photovoltaic power as inputs. A meteorological temporal encoder and a cloud-image spatial encoder are constructed to extract the temporal evolution of irradiance, temperature, humidity, wind speed, and historical power, as well as cloud texture, cloud boundary, and inter-frame cloud variation. An adaptive cross-modal gated fusion module is introduced to dynamically adjust the contribution of meteorological and cloud-image features under different weather states. To improve the learning of rare but operationally important disturbance samples, a disturbance-weighted loss and physical ramp and solar-altitude constraints are further incorporated. Results Experimental results based on chronologically partitioned measured photovoltaic and meteorological data show that the proposed model reduces RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and ramp tracking error compared with baseline models. Discussion The study focuses on forecasting accuracy and ramp-tracking capability, while grid-control effects are discussed only as potential applications requiring further closed-loop validation.

title: Mental bootstrapping enables human-level concept learning in self-supervised deep models
abstract: How agents acquire abstract concepts from sparse, diverse examples-often without explicit supervision-remains a central problem in cognitive science and artificial intelligence. Human studies suggest that this ability depends on mental bootstrapping, the gradual construction of complex concepts from simpler partial structures. Building on this idea, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains models on systematically simplified versions of abstract reasoning tasks containing incomplete but structured concept cues. This algorithm enables models to form internal abstractions under limited resources and later apply them to more complex problems. We evaluate the framework across 12 abstract visual reasoning datasets testing in-distribution concept induction, out-of-distribution generalization, and few-shot learning. To contextualize performance, we also measure human accuracy on the same tasks. Models trained on simplified problems generalize robustly, reaching or even surpassing human-level performance. These findings show that abstract reasoning can emerge from structured simplification and minimal data, offering a computational account of concept learning in humans and machines.

title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: experimental demonstration on MAST Upgrade
abstract: Conventional plasma shape control in tokamaks relies on virtual circuits (VCs) that are computed offline from linearisations around a small, tailored number of reference equilibria, and deployed as expertly prepared schedules during the discharge. Here, we report on the first experimental deployment of real-time VCs. We replace pre-set look up tables with VCs updated in real time using surrogates of the plasma response. Both the existing control architecture and the interpretability of VC-based control are retained. Previous work showed that neural network emulators can produce accurate VCs, and validated their performance in closed-loop shape control simulations. Here, we report their first experimental validation on MAST Upgrade (MAST-U). Dedicated experiments spanning different scenarios, including prescribed shape perturbations, feedback-driven divertor-leg motion, and strongly evolving plasma configurations, show that real-time VCs can realise plasma shape control tasks within the MAST-U plasma control system. These results establish the experimental feasibility of real-time linearisations as a practical extension of conventional plasma shape control in tokamaks. The present implementation demonstrates a central step towards a simpler control workflow, in which manually constructed, phased VC schedules are replaced by VCs generated automatically online from a trained surrogate model, without scenario-specific retraining.

title: Logical Operators and Derived Automorphisms of Tile Codes
abstract: The recently introduced tile codes are a promising alternative to surface codes, combining two-dimensional locality with higher encoding efficiency. While surface codes are well understood in terms of their logical operators and boundary behavior, much less is known about tile codes. In this work, we establish a natural and precise description of their logical operator space. We prove that, under mild assumptions, any tile code admits a canonical symplectic basis of logical operators supported along lattice boundaries, which can be generated efficiently by a simple cellular automaton with the number of update rules only depending on the non-locality of the tile code. Further, we develop algebraic and algebro-geometric frameworks for tile codes, by resolving them by translationally invariant Pauli stabilizer models and showing that they arise as derived sections of a Koszul complex on $$\mathbb {P}^1 \times \mathbb {P}^1$$ . Finally, we introduce the concept of derived automorphisms for quantum codes. These are automorphism-like operations that can exist even for codes that do not have symmetries. We explain how derived automorphisms can be implemented for tile codes in a low-overhead and fault-tolerant manner by extending the lattice on one side and shrinking it on the other. While this operation is trivial for the surface code, it induces a product of logical CNOT gates on the encoded information. Our results provide new structural insights into tile codes and lay the groundwork for tile codes as building blocks for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: The Immediate Nature of Quantum Security Technology, Finance, Private Equity and Family Allocations A Predictive Idea Note — Volume II
abstract: Volume I argued that post-quantum cryptography (PQC / PPQC) is a change of locks, and that the archive will fork into physical and biological media by 2030–2035. This second volume treats the immediate layer: what is already operationally true in late August 2026 for technology, for the financial system, and for private capital. Immediacy here is not a claim that a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists. It is the claim that harvest-now-decrypt-later collection is live; that Mosca's inequality is already failed for long-lived financial and family records; that vendor, HSM and FIPS gates in 2026–2027 will decide who can transact with serious counterparties; and that private equity and family offices are allocating as if quantum were either a listed lottery ticket or a distant IT project — both errors. The note maps the technology that can be bought this year, the financial-system doctrine now issued by the G7, BIS, U.S. Treasury, HKMA, FINMA, Taiwan FSC and RBI, and a barbell allocation for PE and family businesses that separates defensive crypto-agility spend from speculative compute exposure.
