title: Causal Bayesian Networks for Medical Diagnosis
abstract: This paper explores the application of Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to medical diagnosis, addressing the limitations of traditional Bayesian Networks in complex clinical scenarios. The core argument is that CBNs, by explicitly modeling causal relationships, provide a more robust and interpretable framework for diagnostic reasoning. We detail the construction of a CBN representing the causal connections between symptoms, diseases, and potential treatments. Utilizing causal inference techniques, we demonstrate how to reason about the effects of interventions, leading to improved diagnostic accuracy. The approach offers a significant advancement over conventional Bayesian Networks, particularly in situations involving confounding variables and the need for causal interpretation. This work highlights the potential of CBNs to revolutionize medical diagnosis and treatment planning.

title: Semantic Product Similarity im deutschsprachigen E-Commerce
abstract: Die Kenntnis geeigneter Produktalternativen ist insbesondere für E-Commerce-Unternehmen mit umfangreichen Sortimenten von zentraler Bedeutung. Die Größe und Dynamik des Sortiments sowie eine unzureichende Datenbasis erschweren jedoch oftmals deren Identifikation. Die vorliegende Arbeit entwickelt und evaluiert daher ein Verfahren zur Identifikation von Produktalternativen, das ausschließlich auf textuellen Produktinformationen basiert und ohne annotierte Trainingsdaten auskommt. Dazu werden deutschsprachige Produkttexte eines mittelständischen E-Commerce-Unternehmens mit vortrainierten Sentence-Transformer-Modellen in Embeddings überführt. Anschließend werden über eine Ähnlichkeitssuche semantisch ähnliche Produkte bestimmt und durch nachgelagerte Filter um Produktvarianten und Komplementärprodukte bereinigt. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass die Kombination aus Bezeichnung und Beschreibung die stärkste untersuchte Eingabevariante bildet. Vortrainierte Sentence-Transformer identifizieren relevante Alternativen auf einem praktisch nutzbaren, aber begrenzten Präzisionsniveau. Produktvarianten lassen sich dabei zuverlässig abgrenzen, Komplementärprodukte hingegen nur eingeschränkt.

title: Robust model-based clustering via mixtures of multivariate pseudo-Voigt distributions
abstract: We propose a multivariate extension of the pseudo-Voigt profile—a weighted convex combination of Gaussian and Cauchy distributions—within a finite mixture modeling framework for robust model-based clustering and outlier detection. To ensure parsimony and coherence within clusters, shared location and scale parameters are imposed between the Gaussian and Cauchy components. Parameter estimation is carried out via an Expectation Maximization algorithm, with latent variables facilitating efficient likelihood-based inference. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated through simulation studies and applications to real-world data. Comparisons with established robust models, including mixtures of contaminated normal distributions, are provided to illustrate the model’s clustering accuracy and outlier detection capabilities. The framework is shown to be particularly effective for data characterized by heavy-tailed behavior.

title: Descoberta de Conhecimento por Filogenia, Difusão e Fronteiras de Pareto em Cenários de Baixa Rotulagem
abstract: O cenário contemporâneo de Big Data evoluiu de um desafio focado em volume para uma complexidade marcada pela variedade e heterogeneidade das fontes de dados. Neste contexto, a escassez de dados rotulados e a inviabilidade de anotação por especialistas impõem barreiras severas aos métodos tradicionais de Aprendizado de Máquina. Esta tese investiga a hipótese de que a estrutura topológica dos dados, revelada através da análise filogenética e da otimização multiobjetivo, atua como um prior estrutural agnóstico em relação ao domínio capaz de mitigar tais limitações. A pesquisa propõe um arcabouço metodológico unificado fundamentado em três contribuições principais. Primeiramente, aborda-se a inconsistência na propagação de rótulos em Aprendizado Semissupervisionado através do método PhyDL (Phylogram-based Data Labeling). Ao integrar a detecção de comunidades em árvores filogenéticas (construídas via Neighbor Joining) com algoritmos de difusão em grafos, o método corrige erros de classificação em fronteiras de decisão tênues, demonstrando robustez superior em bases de dados com geometria complexa. Em segundo lugar, enfrenta-se o problema do Cold-Start em Aprendizado Ativo com o desenvolvimento do PhyIL (Phylogram-based Initial Labeling). O método substitui a seleção aleatória ou baseada em incerteza (inexistente no início do processo) pela centralidade filogenética, selecionando amostras representativas que maximizam a diversidade do espaço de características sem a necessidade de um modelo prévio. Por fim, a tese apresenta o framework HERMES (Heterogeneous Ensemble Ranking for Modelfree Early Selection), desenhado para atuar sobre dados heterogêneos na ausência total de oráculos. Utilizando a Fronteira de Pareto para ranquear dados não estruturados, o framework infere classes latentes nos extremos de dominância e propaga rótulos de forma autônoma. Um protocolo de validação de estabilidade, baseado em métricas de Flip-Rate e Taxa de Concordância, foi desenvolvido para calibrar os hiperparâmetros de difusão sem a necessidade de rótulos reais. A aplicação do framework em um estudo de caso real sobre Insegurança Alimentar na cidade de São Paulo demonstrou sua capacidade de traduzir dados socioeconômicos brutos em mapas de vulnerabilidade acionáveis para políticas públicas.

title: Hypernetwork-guided fusion with intra-class MixUp for breast cancer subtyping
abstract: Accurate breast cancer subtyping guides treatment selection, yet histopathology captures morphology without molecular state, while genomic profiling captures molecular signatures without spatial context. Existing fusion methods rely on concatenation, or on attention applied only after each modality is encoded independently. This work identifies a scale-dependent asymmetry in the direction of cross-modal conditioning: the direction that performs best under limited samples is not the one that holds at scale, and the reversal is traced to the capacity of the modulation pathway rather than to the fusion principle. The comparison is carried out within a hypernetwork-guided framework in which an auxiliary network maps one modality to conditioning parameters that modulate the other's feature representation, shaping features at the parametric level rather than the decision stage; modulation is patient-specific rather than patch-specific. Both directions are instantiated-gene-to-image (HyperG2I) and image-to-gene (HyperI2G) - and trained under a label-aware MixUp strategy that interpolates within-class samples across both modalities, preserving the hard binary labels clinical decisions require. The framework is evaluated on two paired TCGA-BRCA cohorts-one limited-sample, one independently assembled at scale-under a single protocol spanning two whole-slide representations, multiple visual backbones, and both conditioning directions. On the limited-sample cohort, gene-to-image conditioning at its optimal augmentation setting exceeds early fusion and both unimodal baselines, giving the highest recall on the aggressive Basal/HER2 class of any configuration evaluated, and an ablation favours intra-class over inter-class mixing. At scale this ordering does not hold: image-to-gene conditioning sustains its performance whereas gene-to-image does not, recovering only partially under the full tissue bag and isolating the capacity of the modulation pathway as the binding constraint. Direction and capacity of cross-modal conditioning, rather than fusion depth alone, therefore govern how such frameworks scale.

title: mmIR: Frequency-Space Inverse Rendering for 3D Millimeter-Wave Radar ADC Synthesis
abstract: High-resolution 3D radar data is scarce. Commodity mmWave sensors use small antenna arrays that limit angular resolution to several degrees, and existing datasets provide only 2D range-azimuth maps or sparse point clouds rather than raw analog-to-digital converter (ADC) signals. Hardware scaling is expensive, synthetic-aperture scanning is impractical at fleet scale, and learned synthesis methods are bottlenecked by the very data shortage they aim to address. We present mmIR, an open-source differentiable frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar inverse renderer that fits a physics-based forward model to real captures and re-renders from dense virtual apertures to synthesize high-resolution 3D radar data. Because radar resolution is too coarse to recover geometry directly, mmIR performs LiDAR-assisted inverse rendering: using LiDAR-derived meshes as a geometric scaffold, mmIR optimizes per-vertex International Telecommunication Union (ITU) physics materials, vertex normals, and antenna beam patterns through end-to-end automatic differentiation of a phase-coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) forward model with multi-bounce propagation, polarization, and free-space diffraction. On seven outdoor and six indoor ColoRadar scenes, mmIR achieves 0.914 mean Pearson correlation on range-azimuth maps versus 0.307 for Sionna-RT. Scenes trained on a cascaded imaging radar transfer to a co-located single-chip radar without re-training (0.554 correlation), and dense virtual arrays (100x100 elements) produce single-frame 3D occupancy validated against LiDAR. Project page: https://mmwave-inverse-rendering.github.io/

title: Anatomy-Aware Promptable Segmentation with Online Interactive Training for AUTOPET V
abstract: We present an anatomy-aware, promptable model for whole-body lesion segmentation in FDG and PSMA PET/CT, developed for the AUTOPET V challenge. The proposed method is built as family of nnU-Net-based models and trained in two stages: i) a pre-training stage that produces a strong initial segmentation, and ii) an online interactive stage that learns to exploit scribble prompts, refining the prediction over successive interactions. Anatomical context is incorporated through organ supervision using a single shared head that predicts lesions and organs from the same features, which reduces false positives arising from physiological uptake. Also as the tracer (i.e., FDG/PSMA) is not provided at inference, we add a tracer classifier based on image processing and a random forest over coronal MIP features, routing each study to a combined FDG+PSMA model or to a PSMA-specific model. Across four-fold cross-validation the organ-supervised model achieves the best and most stable performance, the interactive stage improves the Dice score monotonically with each prompt, and PSMA-specific training yields the strongest tracer-wise results.

title: One Pipeline, Many Transformers: Pattern-Specific Imputation Specialists for Tabular Missing Data
abstract: Missing data in tabular datasets forces practitioners into a hard choice: deploy a general-purpose imputer that may perform poorly for the problem at hand, or wait for someone to design a specialized algorithm. This problem is worsened by the fact that real-world missingness rarely satisfies the textbook missing completely at random (MCAR) assumption, as entries are often missing not at random (MNAR), where the probability of being observed depends on the missing data itself. We collapse this trade-off into a single pre-training pipeline that builds transformer-based imputation specialists through three components: an entry-wise featurization that recasts imputation as supervised prediction over row--column context, a synthetic data generator with pluggable missingness modules, and prior-data fitting on millions of synthetic tables. Swapping only the missingness module, with no changes to architecture, loss, or training, yields a pattern-specific specialist that outperforms methods purpose-built for that pattern. We validate this on MissBench, a new benchmark of 42 OpenML datasets and 11 missingness patterns (including 9 MNAR variants) spanning medicine, finance, and engineering. Remarkably, training exclusively on MCAR yields a default model---TabImpute---robust across all tested patterns. In addition, the pattern-specific specialists produced by our pipeline outperform the 14 established baselines on their target patterns. We open-source the pipeline, models, and benchmark.

title: Intelligent Text-Matching System for Compliance Verification of Commercial Vehicles in Active and Passive Safety Research
abstract: The compliance verification of operating vehicles, also known as the verification of compliant vehicles, is a crucial link in ensuring road transportation safety. However, the traditional manual interpretation of the complex remarks in the announcement of compliant vehicle models suffers from low efficiency and is prone to errors. Therefore, this study proposes a multi-level intelligent text matching (MLITM) system framework to automatically determine whether text fragments comply with and explain the differences between the actual vehicles and the parameters in the announcement during the verification process. Methodologically, MLITM adopts a three-level collaborative strategy: rapid filtering through full-text matching; detection of high-similarity segments through the longest common substring matching; and recall of scattered keywords through adaptive sliding window matching. Experiments show that the matching accuracy of MLITM on the simulation dataset is 103.4% higher than that of the regular expression method, with an average processing time of only 26 microseconds and an efficiency improvement of 26 times; among all methods compared in this study, MLITM achieves the best recognition accuracy and recall for various typical samples. Furthermore, by encapsulating the core MLITM algorithm as a microservice module and integrating it into an actual vehicle compliance review system, this study verifies that the proposed method can effectively assist auditors in rapidly locating supporting textual evidence. The results demonstrate its significant potential for improving review efficiency and enhancing the consistency of review outcomes.This system framework provides an efficient and interpretable solution for compliance verification, verifying the feasibility of lightweight AI in vertical fields. Additionally, based on the structured vehicle parameter database generated by this study, it can also provide key data support for active and passive safety research such as the prevention of pedal misoperation in electric commercial vehicles.

title: Research on Automatic Construction Algorithm of Ideological and Political Knowledge Graph in Universities Based on Large Language Model
abstract: Addressing the core pain points in current university ideological and political knowledge graph construction—poor domain adaptability of traditional methods, insufficient entity-relation extraction accuracy, weak implicit knowledge mining capabilities, and the difficulty of general-purpose large models adapting to the rigorous knowledge system and semantic norms of the ideological and political field—this paper proposes a hierarchical entity-relation joint extraction and knowledge calibration algorithm (LLM-HERCKA) driven by a large language model for the ideological and political field. First, a dedicated corpus covering four core ideological and political courses in universities and a fine-tuning paradigm are constructed to achieve deep adaptation of the large model to the ideological and political field. Second, a three-layer ontology architecture for ideological and political knowledge and a hierarchical joint extraction mechanism are designed to solve the error propagation problem of traditional pipeline methods. Finally, a dual-path knowledge calibration module is proposed to ensure the compliance and factual accuracy of extracted knowledge. Experiments were conducted on a self-constructed dataset of 2000 labeled samples for ideological and political education evaluation. Results show that the algorithm achieves an F1 score of 94.27% for entity extraction and 92.58% for relation extraction, representing improvements of 8.35 and 9.76 percentage points respectively compared to the traditional BERT+CRF model, and improvements of 5.12 and 6.34 percentage points respectively compared to the zero-sample extraction of general large-scale models. Ablation experiments validated the effectiveness of each core module. This algorithm can achieve efficient and automated construction of ideological and political knowledge graphs in universities, providing core technical support for digital teaching and intelligent applications of ideological and political education.

abstract: Paper 9 of 11 — A General Theory of Answerability The eleven-paper TUS OS mathematical research programme Abstract This paper develops a general mathematical theory of Answerability as a constituted, typed relation and establishes laws governing its lawful transformation, resource representation, repair, composition, activation, obstruction and conservation. Its governing result is the Base Theorem of Answerability: Answerability is a constituted, typed relation. No terminal proposition counts as an answer unless it lawfully discharges the independently constituted contract. A typed Answerability problem therefore fixes its semantic frame and contract, admitted realisation category, resource structure and tolerance regime before candidate success or optimisation is inspected. This preserves distinct levels of semantic satisfiability, admitted-category realisability and budgeted feasibility, preventing terminal truth, implementation existence and resource affordability from being silently identified. The paper develops a lawful reduction calculus with separately typed semantic transformations, operational lifts and resource lifts; standalone and contextual equivalence; and a contract–resource representation theory based on exact attained resources and principal-budget feasibility. Under explicit generation hypotheses, the complete lower-budget geometry admits extremal reconstruction from irreducible frontiers. Lawful repair is set-valued in general, with a canonical greatest repair only on a stronger order-theoretic branch. Typed composition is then introduced through independent semantic, operational and resource data. Structural activation is defined by genuinely new mandatory composite obligations and is kept distinct from resource activation. Independent obstruction certificates provide the bridge from new obligations to resource consequences, yielding exact feasible-resource activation only under additional stated comparison conditions. The resulting theory allows structural activation without resource penalty, resource advantage without structural activation, and incomparable multi-resource composition regimes. The impossibility theory closes the same object from the opposite direction. Capability and obstruction form a complementary principal-budget geometry: lawful reductions transport feasibility forward and obstruction contravariantly backward. title: Littéracie IA - Parcours pour les gestionnaires
abstract: Comprendre, configurer et piloter l'IA en entreprise, quinze leçons construites pour un lecteur curieux, sans prérequis technique.Ce parcours est né d'un constat répété sur le terrain : la plupart des organisations avancent sur l'IA sans vocabulaire commun ni repère de maturité partagé entre dirigeants, équipes techniques et utilisateurs métier, ce qui ralentit les décisions et multiplie les faux départs. Trencadis a offert un cadre de développement de ce parcours durant 4 mois et permis une collaboration féconde entre deux générations de praticiens. Plutôt que de garder cette pédagogie interne, Trencadis a choisi d'en publier une version ouverte : donner à toute organisation les mots et les repères nécessaires pour discuter d'IA avec la même rigueur qu'un autre sujet stratégique. Ce parcours est comme une plateforme vivante : il existe en ligne, sa structure est robuste et durable, et il permettra des mises à jour régulières pour rester en prise avec un sujet qui évolue de façon significative au rythme de la semaine.Le chef de projet IA porte une attention particulière portée à la fiabilité, à la mesure de la performance et à la gouvernance des solutions qu'il met en place. La double compétence, technique et gestion de projet, irrigue directement le contenu du parcours : chaque notion y est présentée avec le niveau d'exigence attendu d'une mise en production réelle, pas d'une démonstration. Le senior advisor cumule 35 ans d'expérience en organisation d'entreprise, au service de plus de 120 organisations de toutes tailles et de tous secteurs. Cette pratique de terrain, acquise bien avant l'arrivée de l'IA générative, est ce qui structure l'approche du parcours : l'IA y est traitée comme un sujet d'organisation avant d'être un sujet technique, gouvernance, rôles, processus, capacités humaines, plutôt que comme une simple question d'outillage Bonne lectureContact : fgaurier@trencadis.ca

title: 基于量子纠缠的分布式语义理解
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic understanding and reasoning by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional semantic understanding methods face limitations due to the inherent constraints of classical computation and centralized data storage. This research introduces a distributed system designed to overcome these limitations, utilizing pre-entangled quantum bits to enable real-time perception of correlations between data elements, regardless of their physical separation. The system employs quantum graph algorithms for inference, capitalizing on the non-local nature of entanglement to achieve higher data processing capabilities and potentially faster reasoning speeds. The core claim is that by harnessing entanglement's non-locality, we can construct a system capable of distributed semantic understanding and reasoning that surpasses the boundaries of traditional computation. The key mechanism involves a network of quantum processors, each handling a portion of the semantic data, connected through entangled qubits. We detail the architecture, the quantum graph algorithm implementation, and discuss the challenges and future directions of this technology.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Time Synchronization
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility and potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for distributed time synchronization. We propose a novel framework leveraging multi-body quantum entanglement to achieve highly precise and secure time synchronization beyond the limitations imposed by classical physics. The core mechanism involves constructing a distributed network of quantum sensors interconnected through entangled states. By measuring the phase shifts within these entangled states and exploiting the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to mitigate error propagation, we demonstrate the possibility of accurately synchronizing the time of all sensors in the network. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional methods reliant on classical communication, providing enhanced security and precision. The research highlights the potential for applications requiring ultra-precise timing, such as fundamental physics experiments, advanced sensor networks, and secure communication protocols. We introduce a theoretical model outlining the synchronization process and discuss key challenges and future research directions. ---

title: Causality-Driven Reasoning Framework for Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) centered around causality-driven reasoning. The core claim is that understanding and leveraging causal relationships within data is crucial for building truly interpretable and trustworthy AI models. The framework integrates causal graph modeling, counterfactual reasoning, and machine learning algorithms to learn causal structures directly from data. This approach moves beyond purely correlational explanations, offering a more robust and meaningful way to understand model decisions. We demonstrate the potential of this framework through a theoretical exploration, highlighting its advantages in scenarios where spurious correlations are prevalent. The resulting system provides a pathway towards XAI models that are not only explainable but also grounded in a genuine understanding of the underlying phenomena.

title: Cognitive Architecture-Based Agent Design
abstract: This paper explores the design and development of intelligent agents grounded in cognitive architectures. The core claim is that accurately simulating human cognition within an agent framework significantly enhances learning and reasoning capabilities. This work proposes a mechanism centered on constructing a cognitive architecture, comprised of modular components mirroring human cognitive processes – perception, memory, and reasoning – within the agent's core. The architecture then serves as a guiding framework for agent behavior. Unlike traditional rule-based and experience-driven agents, this approach aims to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and human cognition, ultimately leading to more adaptable and intelligent systems. The presented design offers a robust foundation for future research and development in intelligent agent design, particularly in areas requiring complex decision-making and learning. ---

title: Lightweight programmable microring resonator photonic convolutional neural network for modulation format classification
abstract: Despite the rapid progress of on-chip photonic computing, optical neural networks (ONNs) remain constrained by limited kernel expressivity, weak nonlinearities, and substantial hardware overhead. To address these limitations, we propose a compact microring resonator (MRR)-based photonic convolutional neural network (PCNN) for modulation format classification from constellation diagrams. This architecture is based on cascaded dual-microring units and add–drop MRRs; the former achieves dual-port mixing in the optical linear layer through a phase compensation mechanism while the latter utilizes differential pass-through and up/down-link readout to implement signed convolution kernel coefficients. On constellation diagrams derived from the RML2016.10a dataset, the proposed PCNN achieves accuracies of 82.58%, 87.85%, and 91.94% at input resolutions of 16×16, 32×32, and 48×48, respectively, with only 0.25 million trainable parameters and 0.001 GFLOPs. We further provide an explicit physics-to-network parameter mapping and a first-order implementation-budget analysis, indicating a compact and programmable photonic route to modulation format recognition under tight computational and hardware budgets.

title: HEAR what AI says: simulated empathy and supportive ChatGPT interaction for emotional well-being
abstract: This study explores how simulated empathy can function as an emotionally supportive interaction feature in users’ ongoing engagement with ChatGPT for emotional support. As AI-powered chatbots increasingly appear in emotionally sensitive situations, understanding how users relate to them as emotionally supportive conversational partners becomes important. Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, the Technology Acceptance Model, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour, this study develops and empirically examines an integrative HEAR framework. The framework examines how users’ perceptions of empathic communication, human-likeness, and ease of use influence both cognitive evaluations and affective responses, including emotional comfort and usage disposition. Data from 892 users who had used ChatGPT to express emotions were analysed using structural equation modelling. The results show that perceived empathic communication plays a central role in shaping emotional comfort and trust, while human-likeness strongly predicts how emotionally safe users feel during interaction. These emotional factors, in turn, significantly affect users’ intention to continue using ChatGPT. Notably, users may experience ChatGPT as an emotionally supportive listener, not because it experiences emotions, but because it responds in ways that make people feel understood. By positioning empathy as more than a design feature, this study highlights ChatGPT’s emerging role in digital wellbeing contexts.

title: SemKV: Semantic Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization Guided by the Quality Cliff for Long-Context LLM Inference
abstract: The key-value (KV) cache is the dominant memory bottleneck of long-context large language model (LLM) inference, growing linearly with context length. We show that uniform KV quantization on a fractional-bit grid does not degrade gracefully: under a prespecified multi-seed statistical protocol, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with an affine quantizer is statistically indistinguishable from FP16 KV down to 2.322 code bits/value and collapses at 2.0 bits - a quality cliff in (2.0, 2.322] that reappears in generation-time quantization and multi-turn dialogue and transfers to Mistral-7B. The cliff reframes importance-aware mixed precision: above it, eight model-internal importance indicators are statistically interchangeable, so the benefit of mixing is grid interpolation, reaching average precisions uniform quantization cannot realize. SemKV preserves every token, ranks tokens by a model-internal score, and assigns two adjacent above-cliff precisions, achieving a measured 6.0x storage reduction with no statistically detectable quality difference from full KV (n=900, three seeds), and outperforming FP16 token pruning granted a 1.5x larger memory budget. Replacing the affine base with a distortion-optimized quantizer (TurboQuant-MSE) lowers the cliff in every protocol tested, raising the no-detectable-loss operating point to 7.9x. The recipe: measure the cliff for the target deployment setting, then interpolate above it.

title: Vacuum-selected timescales in driven Josephson systems
abstract: Abstract In this work, we demonstrate that the intrinsic timescale of a Josephson junction can be controlled through dynamical vacuum selection. By applying a Kapitza-like high-frequency drive to the system, the effective Josephson potential is reshaped, allowing for the stabilization of inphase or antiphase configuration. As a result, the Josephson plasma frequency, that is, the clock frequency of the junction, becomes a tunable property of the selected vacuum. Our findings establish a vacuum-controlled Josephson clock principle, in which the dynamical vacuum acts as an internal reference that fixes the operational timescale of Josephson oscillations, rather than this scale being imposed externally. Our results open a route toward a vacuum-controlled temporal functionality in Josephson systems, where the intrinsic dynamical timescale is determined by the configuration around which the phase dynamics is organized.

title: An Empirical Study on Zero-Data Bootstrapping for Conversational Recommender Systems
abstract: Conversational Recommender Systems (CRS) typically require domain-specific dialogue data, which is costly, scarce, and often unavailable in new domains. We conduct a systematic empirical study of zero-data CRS bootstrapping: generating synthetic conversational supervision from non-conversational signals---item reviews, metadata, and user-item interactions---without any in-domain dialogue corpus. We compare two information-theoretic selection strategies, Jensen-Shannon diversity and Fisher information, across domain signals, model architectures, datasets, and fine-tuning paradigms. Our results show that domain-grounded synthetic data consistently outperforms zero-shot prompting and naive synthetic baselines; active selection improves data efficiency over random sampling; metadata and collaborative filtering signals each improve selection quality; and, in low-resource settings, synthetic data can outperform scarce real dialogues while further complementing them. These findings establish non-conversational domain signals as a viable path toward building CRS without conversational training data. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/zero_data_crs/ .

title: ROBÓTICA EDUCACIONAL COM ARDUINO: CONSTRUÇÃO DE UM PROTÓTIPO ANTICOLISÃO COMO ESTRATÉGIA PARA O DESENVOLVIMENTO DO PENSAMENTO COMPUTACIONAL E FORMAÇÃO DOCENTE
abstract: This work discusses a robotics proposal for education using the Arduino to build an anti-collision robot. The research work is divided into two parts: assembling the robot hardware and programming the software that governs its commands. This proposal is divided into two stages: the first as a pedagogical methodology for teaching students; the second, an educational product that offers assistance in continuing training for the teacher, as support for content development.

title: Private Brains: Retrieval-Grounded Enterprise AI Without Data Egress
abstract: An enterprise assistant is only as useful as its access to the organisation's own knowledge, yet the common way of providing that access, sending documents and their embeddings to a cloud service for indexing and retrieval, reintroduces exactly the data-egress problem that regulated organisations must avoid. This paper describes a retrieval architecture in which an organisation's knowledge is held in private knowledge bases, which we call brains, on hardware the organisation owns, and is made available to an offline assistant without any data leaving the building. Ingestion, indexing, routing and retrieval all run locally. A routing layer selects the brains relevant to a query and retrieves only the material needed, so that a single prompt's working context stays within the served model's context window while large corpora remain usable. We have exercised retrieval over a 41 GB reference corpus on a single workstation, which indicates that corpus size is bounded by local storage rather than by an external service. Retrieved sources are recorded in the system's attestation record, so that it can be shown after the fact which knowledge informed a given answer. We contrast the approach with cloud retrieval-augmented generation and discuss its operational and regulatory implications.

title: 延标延时闭合推演体系:面向不完备约束系统的元认知推演体系
abstract: 针对“逻辑框架可形式化建构,但关键参量真值暂不可获取”的不完备约束认知场景,本文提出延标延时闭合推演体系。该体系以延标变量 X(\infty) 为形式载体,通过元注释标签显式区分已知条件与待闭合未知参量,确立禁止无依据强制坍缩、事实驱动闭合、推演结构留存、闭合参数归档复用核心原则。体系允许认知悬置,拒绝主观编造定值与置信度,将推演重心从即时求解确定结果转向识别认知缺口、设计验证路径、等待客观事实回填真值。该范式能够抑制AI强制坍缩诱发的幻觉,为通用智能实现“知其不知”、生成内生认知补全驱动力提供形式化基础,可应用于科学假说、工程仿真、政策研判与复杂系统建模。

title: Quantum Accelerated Computation via Entangled Teleportation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hardware acceleration of specific computational tasks leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and quantum teleportation. The core idea is to decompose complex calculations into a series of entangled qubit operations, facilitated by quantum teleportation, thereby achieving significant speedups. We outline a framework for designing and implementing such accelerators, focusing on the efficiency and scalability of this method. The proposed architecture aims to bypass traditional computational bottlenecks by directly exploiting the inherent parallelism of quantum mechanics. This work establishes a theoretical foundation for quantum teleportation-based hardware acceleration, offering a promising direction for future quantum computing advancements. The key metrics for evaluating performance – speedup and fidelity – are explicitly discussed. ---

title: Graph Neural Networks with Hierarchical Relational Reasoning
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. However, many existing GNN architectures struggle to effectively capture complex relationships within graphs, particularly those exhibiting hierarchical structures. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance GNNs by integrating hierarchical relational reasoning. Our core claim is that GNNs can be significantly improved by explicitly modeling dependencies across multiple levels of graph abstraction. We introduce a GNN architecture designed to decompose graphs into a hierarchy of subgraphs, each representing a different level of abstraction. These subgraphs are then processed sequentially, allowing the model to capture increasingly nuanced relationships. The novelty of our approach lies in the explicit modeling of hierarchical relationships within graphs, addressing the limitations of traditional GNNs. We define the following key elements: (G = (V, E), where V is the set of nodes and E is the set of edges); (si, sj) representing a connection between nodes i and j; (H = {H1, H2, ..., HL}) representing the hierarchical structure of the graph, where Hl is the l-th level of hierarchy; (fl(Hl)) representing the function that processes the subgraphs at level l; and (overall_loss = Σl=1L lossl) representing the total loss. The proposed method aims to minimize this overall loss by effectively learning the hierarchical relationships within the graph.

title: Explainable AI for Quantum Circuit Optimization using Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuit optimization is crucial for realizing the full potential of quantum computing, but current optimization techniques often operate as black boxes, lacking transparency and hindering trust. This paper proposes a novel approach combining tensor networks with explainable AI to address this challenge. We represent quantum circuits using tensor networks, allowing for a richer mathematical representation and facilitating the application of explainable AI methods. The developed system generates visualizations and textual explanations detailing the key factors driving optimization decisions, promoting understanding and trust in the process. The core claim highlights the critical need for explainability in AI-driven optimization, while the proposed mechanism leverages tensor networks to achieve this. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach to enhance transparency and accelerate the adoption of quantum circuit optimization techniques. This work introduces a new paradigm for quantum optimization, moving beyond opaque algorithms towards interpretable and trustworthy solutions.

title: Formal Representation of Semantic Networks using Tensor Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to representing and reasoning with semantic networks utilizing the power of tensor networks. Traditional semantic network representation struggles with scalability and efficient inference, particularly when dealing with complex relationships. We propose a mapping strategy where the nodes and edges of a semantic network are directly translated into tensor elements, creating a tensor network representation. This allows for parallel computation of relationships and inferences, offering potential improvements in both computational efficiency and scalability. We demonstrate the core mechanism through mathematical formulation, outlining the tensor network construction and inference rules. The key contribution lies in applying tensor network theory to the domain of knowledge representation, opening new avenues for sophisticated reasoning and knowledge management. The framework presented herein provides a foundation for developing more efficient and scalable semantic network systems.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Models: Design and Validation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing and validating explainable deep learning models. The core challenge in modern deep learning is the lack of interpretability, often leading to "black box" models that are difficult to trust and understand. This work addresses this issue by proposing a framework centered around incorporating mechanisms that enhance model explainability, primarily through rule-based approaches or attention mechanisms, alongside establishing verifiable explanations. The key contribution lies in building a systematic approach to not only generate explanations but also to rigorously validate their accuracy and consistency. We explore various techniques for representing explanations and introduce a method for quantifying the confidence in the generated explanations. The ultimate goal is to move towards deep learning models that are both accurate and transparent, facilitating broader adoption in critical applications where trust and accountability are paramount. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a potential implementation strategy.

title: Formal Semantic-Based Program Synthesis with Type Reasoning
abstract: Program synthesis, the automatic generation of executable code from high-level specifications, faces a significant challenge in ensuring the type safety and maintainability of the synthesized programs. Traditional approaches often rely on heuristics or incomplete type information, leading to errors and difficulties in debugging. This paper proposes a novel framework for program synthesis incorporating formal semantic techniques, specifically focusing on automated type reasoning. Our core claim is to design a system capable of performing type inference during the synthesis process, thereby enhancing the type safety and maintainability of the generated code. The proposed mechanism leverages formal type systems and dedicated type inference algorithms to rigorously check and reason about the types of the synthesized programs. We demonstrate that this approach effectively addresses the core problem of type inference in program synthesis, leading to more reliable and robust software solutions. The system operates by translating the input specification into a formal representation and then utilizing a sophisticated type inference engine to deduce the appropriate types for each construct in the synthesized program. The process is iterative, refining the program and its type information until a complete and type-correct solution is achieved. This work contributes to a more practical and dependable program synthesis paradigm.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning from Simulated Physics
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains by learning from unlabeled data. However, many current SSL methods necessitate large amounts of real-world data, which can be costly to acquire, often limited in quantity and diversity, and may contain biases. This paper proposes a novel approach to SSL by leveraging the abundance and controllability of simulated physics environments. We train representation learning models using data generated from physics engines, allowing for the creation of robust and generalizable representations. The core claim is that training on simulated physics offers a viable and potentially superior alternative to real-world data for SSL. The core mechanism involves utilizing the rich, controllable data generated by physics simulations. This approach opens up a new avenue for SSL, reducing the dependence on real-world data and its associated challenges. We explore the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and demonstrate its potential for improved representation learning.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in Healthcare, Industries, and Everyday Life
abstract: This paper examines the role of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in modern society, with a focus on healthcare, industry, and everyday life. It explores how AI supports decision-making, data analysis, and intelligent responses, while Robotics enables machines to perform physical tasks with accuracy and consistency. Based on secondary sources, the study follows a descriptive and analytical approach. The paper highlights the growing usefulness of AI and Robotics, along with concerns related to privacy, bias, employment, safety, and access. It argues that these technologies should be developed responsibly, with human supervision, ethical design, and inclusive use.

title: High-Dimensional Outlier Detection Methods
abstract: This chapter provides an overview of high-dimensional outlier detection methods, addressing the challenges posed when https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> d ≫ N . Traditional techniques, including Mahalanobis distance-based approaches, are sensitive to outliers and often fail in high-dimensional settings due to singularity of the covariance matrix and masking or swamping effects. To overcome these limitations, robust estimators such as the minimum covariance determinant, minimum volume ellipsoid, and component-wise medians are discussed. Proximity-based methods, including IPDs , nearest-neighbor approaches, and kernel-based outlier factors, offer distribution-free alternatives while retaining sensitivity to anomalies. The chapter also examines generalized dispersion measures, r-th nearest neighbor methods, and bootstrap-based procedures for assessing statistical significance. Performance studies under normal, https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> t 4 , skew-normal, and mixture distributions illustrate the comparative effectiveness of these techniques. Practical applications demonstrate the utility of high-dimensional outlier detection in real-world contexts, including finance, health monitoring, and data mining. Collectively, these methodologies provide a robust, computationally feasible framework for identifying anomalous observations in complex multivariate datasets.

title: Conformal Risk-Averse Decision Making with Optimized Certainty Equivalent Risk Control
abstract: We study risk-averse decision making, in which an agent selects actions while being uncertain about the true system state. The risk is measured via optimized certainty equivalent (OCE) metrics, which generalize popular criteria such as mean-variance risk and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). We characterize the optimal policy under known distributions, and show that it reduces to a prediction set-based solution for the CVaR. This provides an operational interpretation of conformal prediction-type prediction sets. For unknown distributions, we develop a data-driven calibration strategy, based on a synthetic model for the likelihood and held-out calibration data, yielding high-probability control of the OCE risk. The approach is evaluated on two wireless beamforming settings.

title: AI Alignment through a Game-theoretic Lens: A Survey
abstract: As large language models and increasingly capable AI agents are deployed in high-risk settings, aligning them with complex human values has become a central challenge. Existing alignment methods, while effective in improving helpfulness, harmlessness, and controllability, often struggle to capture real-world preferences that are context-dependent, non-transitive, and shaped by dynamic multi-party interactions. This survey reviews AI alignment through a game-theoretic lens. Specifically, it organizes recent progress around key game-theoretic elements and synthesizes the literature along three challenges: preference diversity, alignment priority, and temporal dynamics. This perspective clarifies where current alignment methods genuinely benefit from game-theoretic analysis, where the framework is looser, and what challenges remain in building robust, adaptive, and verifiable AI systems.

title: Quantum interference conventions: Overlap determinability and the unified no-superposition principle
abstract: Quantum superposition is often phrased as the ability to add state vectors. In practice, however, the physical quantity is a ray (a rank-one projector), so each input specifies only a projector and leaves a gauge freedom in the phases of its vector representatives. This becomes a real operational barrier when one asks for a device that, given two independently prepared unknown pure states, outputs a coherent state proportional to a prescribed linear combination. We identify the missing ingredient as not probabilistic but phase-like. One needs a physical scenario that fixes a single phase convention on the relevant set of rays, so that the overlaps become well defined complex numbers. Thus, we formalize this through phase conventions and a single notion -- dubbed as "overlap-determinability." Our main theorem gives an exact equivalence: A nonzero completely positive trace-nonincreasing map that probabilistically produces superposition on a domain exists if and only if that domain is overlap-determinable. This unifies modern no-superposition results and characterizes the exceptional yes-go protocols, which succeed precisely when side information supplies the required missing resource. We then show that granting universal access to such convention-fixed overlaps destabilizes the familiar foundational and computational constraints. It enables forbidden transformations akin to quantum cloning and yields super-luminal signaling. It would also permit reflections about unknown states, leading to exponentially fast overlap amplification and a collapse of Grover's search lower bound to a logarithmic query complexity.

title: RRL-HierProto : Une architecture hiérarchique couplant contexte local et prototypes sémantiques globaux pour l’étiquetage des rôles rhétoriques - code source
abstract: Source code used to conduct the experiments reported in this paper:Anas Belfathi, Nicolas Hernandez, Monceaux Laura, Warren Bonnard, Mary Catherine Lavissière, Christine Jacquin, and Richard Dufour. 2026. Coupling Local Context and Global Semantic Prototypes via a Hierarchical Architecture for Rhetorical Roles Labeling. In Proceedings of the 19th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 2986–3004, Rabat, Morocco. Association for Computational Linguistics.https://aclanthology.org/2026.eacl-long.137/Rhetorical Role Labeling (RRL) identifies the functional role of each sentence in a document, a key task for discourse understanding in domains such as law and medicine. While hierarchical models capture local dependencies effectively, they are limited in modeling global, corpus-level features.We propose two prototype-based methods that integrate local context with global representations:* Prototype-Based Regularization (PBR) — learns soft prototypes through a distance-based auxiliary loss to structure the latent space without altering the backbone architecture.* Prototype-Conditioned Modulation (PCM) — constructs corpus-level prototypes and injects them into the hierarchical encoder during both training and inference.We also introduce SCOTUS-LAW, the first dataset of U.S. Supreme Court opinions annotated with rhetorical roles at three levels of granularity: category, rhetorical function, and step. Experiments on legal, medical, and scientific benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong baselines, with ~4 Macro-F1 gains on low-frequency roles.

title: Evidence bundle for "Deadline-Aware Hardening of Real-Time Object Detection Against Candidate-Inflation Latency Attacks"
abstract: The measurement record behind every number in the paper, with the mapping that tiesthem together and a script that checks it. The manuscript quotes no numeric literal for a measured result. Each carries a claim identifier; claims_registry.yaml records, for that identifier, a source artifact and a dotted pointer into it, and never the value itself; evidence_ledger.json holds the resolved value together with its sample count, timing scope, dataset split, model, runtime, hardware and caveat. This deposit contains the ledger, the registry, all 65 artifacts they point at, the provenance sidecars for the figures, and the deployed model package's own metrics file. verify.py re-resolves every claim against the bundled artifacts and reports any that disagrees. It needs only Python and PyYAML — no dataset, weights, GPU or network. At deposit time all 129 registered claims resolve and agree, 87 of them in the scope the 12-page paper quotes. Not included: the crafted image sets and captured candidate arrays, which are derivatives of VisDrone2019-DET and BDD100K and are redistributed subject to those corpora's terms — available from the corresponding author on request. The attack is deterministic given the seed recorded in the paper. The reference implementation of the defense is a separate record, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22117976.

title: Formal Mathematical Translation of the Empathic Logic Model
abstract: This extension of ELM presents the formal mathematical translation of the Empathic Logic Model (ELM). Because foundational psychological mechanisms and narrative elements function as qualitative components, all related constructs are designated as such; for comprehensive qualitative frameworks, readers can reference the **UNFORMALIZABLE AS WRITTEN** sections documentation in the primary manuscript via Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18614652 ### Note on Mathematical Scope and Evaluation: Mathematical Scope and Operational Interpretation. ELM is an applied computational architecture for dynamic interactive systems, evaluated through operational execution, transition robustness, fault tolerance, and recovery, including adversarial stress testing under Full-Stack Turing Deadlock, PBFT, and ABFT-inspired conditions, rather than abstract mathematical proofs. Its architecture is not intrinsically limited to human–human interaction and may be instantiated in human–machine interaction, machine-learning pipelines, AI safety, robotics, autonomous systems, and other interactive agents, subject to implementation and empirical validation. Artificial intelligence systems were utilized in this formal translation. ### Future Translation Note: Its translation into engineering architectures remains open to domain-specific implementation, with the resulting configurations determined by the requirements and operational constraints of each application field and informed by subsequent empirical development. ### Explanation of this Computational Architecture: ELM governs the interpretation process by determining what the system should do next with received input and how that input should be handled. The input may originate from a sensory parser or other data parser in machine systems, or from biological sensory organs in human beings. By operating directly after the input layer of a system, ELM provides a structured mechanism for managing interpretation toward understanding rather than premature judgment, contextual data rather than static guessing, and the detection and resolution of uncertainty and predictive errors. This includes both preventing and resolving predictive errors—ELM helps identify the triggers of predictive errors and resolve them to prevent the errors from occurring in the first place—as well as helping to resolve predictive errors when others commit them. ELM examines whether the received input contains sufficient contextual information, insufficient contextual information, or distorted contextual information. When contextual information is unavailable or distorted, ELM routes the system toward obtaining or refining the required contextual information through the appropriate contextual-extraction and interaction processes, while maintaining the safeguards specified by the ELM architecture to avoid introducing further predictive errors into the interaction. When the input already contains sufficient contextual information, or when missing contextual information has been obtained through the appropriate extraction and refinement processes established in ELM, ELM subjects the resulting contextual information to the verification and stabilization processes defined by its architecture. When the relevant criteria are satisfied, the resulting information can then be made available to the system for its application-specific purpose. ELM does not impose artificial agreement and does not seek to eliminate disagreement. It prioritizes proportional coherence over certainty, clarity over control, and understanding over judgment. Accordingly, ELM provides an end-to-end computational routing architecture for the interpretation process within the operational scope defined by its formal specification, including contextual assessment, contextual acquisition and refinement, verification, stabilization, state transitions, interruption handling, and recovery. This allows systems such as human beings, corporations, institutions, robots, artificial intelligence systems, machine-learning pipelines, autonomous systems, and other interactive agents to operate on contextually processed and verified information rather than relying solely on static guessing or unverified input, subject to their respective implementation requirements and empirical validation.

title: Probabilistic Logic Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program synthesis – Probabilistic Logic Program Synthesis (PLPS). Traditional program synthesis methods often operate under the assumption of perfect knowledge, neglecting the inherent uncertainty present in real-world applications. PLPS addresses this limitation by directly synthesizing logic programs with probabilistic properties. The core claim is that probabilistic properties should be modeled and synthesized directly, rather than imposed as constraints after synthesis. This work proposes a mechanism utilizing probabilistic models, specifically Bayesian Networks or Variational Inference, to learn the probability distribution governing program behavior, and then leverages this distribution to generate logic programs satisfying specified probabilistic constraints. The novelty lies in the integration of probabilistic reasoning with logic programming, offering a new paradigm for building intelligent systems capable of handling uncertainty. This approach provides a framework for representing and manipulating uncertainty within the logical structure of programs, allowing for the creation of more robust and adaptable systems. The synthesis process is driven by learning from data and probabilistic constraints, resulting in programs that are not only logically correct but also reflect the underlying uncertainty in the problem domain. ---

title: Causal Discovery via Contrastive Learning on Graph Data
abstract: Traditional methods for causal discovery frequently rely on restrictive assumptions regarding data characteristics, significantly limiting their applicability across diverse scenarios. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging contrastive learning for causal discovery on graph data. The core idea involves training a neural network to discern between causal and non-causal relationships within a graph, utilizing a contrastive loss function to achieve this. We posit that this data-driven approach offers increased flexibility and robustness compared to conventional techniques. The proposed method's effectiveness is demonstrated through its ability to learn underlying causal structures from complex datasets without prior assumptions about data distributions or relationships. This research contributes to the field by providing a potentially more accurate and reliable framework for causal inference.

title: Bio-Inspired Deep Graph Neural Network Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to learning from complex graph data by integrating the representation learning capabilities of Deep Graph Neural Networks (DGNs) with the exploratory power of bio-inspired algorithms. The core idea is to construct a DGN where hidden layers employ algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) or Simulated Annealing (SA) to actively search and optimize for hidden patterns and features within the graph data. This hybrid architecture leverages the strengths of both paradigms: DGNs' ability to automatically learn node embeddings and capture local graph structures, and bio-inspired algorithms' capability for global exploration and escaping local optima. The resulting system offers an automated solution for feature extraction and node classification in challenging graph datasets. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline the key components and design considerations. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these techniques, offering a new direction for graph learning research.

title: Based on Quantum Error Correction Codes Dynamic Topological Quantum Storage
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic construction of a quantum storage system leveraging the synergistic capabilities of quantum error correction codes (QECC) and topological quantum storage. The core claim centers on the development of a storage system exhibiting high fault tolerance and extended storage durations. The proposed mechanism integrates QECC protocols with topological quantum storage media, capitalizing on the inherent robustness offered by topological protection to significantly enhance the system's resistance to noise and improve its storage longevity. We explore the theoretical framework and key considerations for implementing such a system, focusing on the interplay between code design, topological protection, and storage dynamics. The approach represents a novel pathway toward practical quantum storage solutions, addressing the critical challenges of decoherence and limited storage times currently hindering quantum information processing. The analysis demonstrates the potential for achieving significantly improved storage performance compared to conventional quantum storage methods. ---

title: Adaptive Defense in Hardware Security Modules for Trusted Computing
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of static defense mechanisms within Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) in the context of Trusted Computing. The core claim is the design of an adaptive defense system capable of dynamically adjusting its security posture based on observed attack patterns within the HSM itself. This system utilizes continuous monitoring and analysis of the HSM's internal state to proactively identify and mitigate emerging threats. The proposed mechanism leverages the HSM's inherent capabilities for real-time attack assessment and automated parameter adjustments, ultimately enhancing defense effectiveness. The novelty lies in moving beyond the static configurations typically employed in HSMs, offering a more responsive and resilient security solution. The system incorporates feedback loops for continuous learning and adaptation, aiming to maintain a robust defense against evolving attack strategies. This approach recognizes that attacks on HSMs are rarely static and necessitate a dynamic response to remain effective. The system will be described in detail, including the architecture, the monitoring and analysis components, and the adaptive parameter adjustment mechanisms. Finally, the potential benefits and challenges of implementing such a system are discussed.

title: Dynamic Programming for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Temporal Abstraction
abstract: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) offers a promising approach to tackling complex decision-making problems by decomposing them into simpler, manageable sub-tasks. However, applying traditional dynamic programming (DP) techniques to HRL architectures faces significant challenges due to the curse of dimensionality. This work presents a novel dynamic programming algorithm tailored for HRL environments, leveraging temporal abstraction layers to effectively reduce the state space and approximate the Bellman equation across multiple levels of abstraction. The core of the approach involves recursively applying DP within each level of the hierarchy, with abstraction layers introducing a coarser representation of the state space at higher levels. This allows for a more tractable computation and a more efficient learning process compared to standard DP methods. We outline the key components of the algorithm, focusing on the design of the temporal abstraction layers and the method for propagating value estimates across the hierarchy. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a detailed discussion of its advantages and limitations.

title: Cognitive Graph Databases for Modeling Human Knowledge
abstract: This paper explores the potential of cognitive graph databases (CGDs) as a novel approach to modeling and reasoning about human knowledge. Traditional relational databases struggle to capture the complex, interconnected nature of human cognition, often relying on rigid schemas and lacking the ability to represent and simulate cognitive processes. Conversely, graph databases excel at representing relationships between entities, and this work proposes integrating these capabilities with established cognitive modeling frameworks. The core concept involves leveraging frameworks like ACT-R and SOAR within a graph database environment to create systems that can not only store knowledge but also simulate cognitive processes such as attention, memory retrieval, and decision-making. This paper outlines the architecture of a CGD, details the integration strategies with cognitive modeling techniques, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges of this approach. The aim is to demonstrate how CGDs can provide a more intuitive and flexible representation of human knowledge, ultimately leading to advancements in areas such as artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and human-computer interaction. The key contribution is a methodology for bridging the gap between data storage and cognitive simulation.

title: Graph-Based Symbolic Regression for Scientific Discovery
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance often degrades significantly when dealing with complex, high-dimensional datasets, limiting its applicability in many scientific domains. This paper introduces a novel graph-based symbolic regression algorithm designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to represent mathematical expressions as graphs, which provides a more efficient and flexible framework for exploring the solution space. This approach allows for the discovery of complex relationships that might be missed by traditional SR methods. The algorithm employs graph traversal and symbolic manipulation to iteratively refine the graph representation and ultimately identify accurate equations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline of the algorithm, highlighting its potential for enhancing the scalability and expressiveness of SR, particularly when confronted with challenging scientific datasets. The key advantages of this method lie in its ability to manage the exponential growth of the search space inherent in traditional SR and its capacity to capture intricate dependencies within multi-variable data.

title: MINAB: A Lightweight 8‐Bit S‐Box With Low Hardware Complexity for Cryptographic Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper, a lightweight S‐box with acceptable cryptographic properties is presented. The proposed S‐box is designed using smaller S‐boxes. Here, we design an 8‐bit S‐box with a nonlinearity of 100 by combining three 4‐bit S‐boxes using SageMath. The 4‐bit S‐boxes have favorable hardware and cryptographic characteristics. By applying algebraic simplifications to the algebraic relations of these S‐boxes, we have arrived at optimized hardware structures for the 4‐bit S‐boxes. This ultimately leads to a reduction in hardware consumption and a decrease in the delay of the proposed 8‐bit S‐box. The proposed structure requires minimal hardware resources while preserving its cryptographic properties. The implementation results using 180‐ and 65‐nm CMOS technologies demonstrate that the proposed S‐box performs comparably in terms of area, delay, and AreaTime when compared to most other works. The proposed S‐box is area‐efficient, making it suitable for lightweight cryptographic applications.

title: Coarse to Fine: Iterative Adversarial Neural Cellular Automata for Medical Image Synthesis
abstract: Large-scale, publicly available datasets have driven advances in deep learning, but privacy and legal restrictions often limit data sharing in medical imaging. Synthetic data generation offers a privacy-friendly alternative to enable the training of high-performance models on health data. While most state-of-the-art generative models produce high-quality images, they remain computationally expensive, which limits their applicability on resource-constrained hardware. We propose StyleGANCA, the first lightweight general-purpose NCA-based generative adversarial network. The architecture integrates a StyleGAN-inspired mapping network and adaptive style modulation into a multi-scale NCA synthesis process, enabling latent-controlled image generation through iterative local interactions. We evaluate StyleGANCA on BloodMNIST and PathMNIST against adversarial, variational, diffusion, and NCA-based baselines. Experimental results demonstrate that StyleGANCA achieves competitive image quality with substantially fewer parameters than baseline architectures, achieving the best FID and KID scores on PathMNIST with only 617k parameters. Furthermore, downstream experiments show that the generated images preserve class-specific information and effectively support the training of multi-class classifiers. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/MECLabTUDA/StyleGANCA

title: Expert Knowledge & Machine Understanding: Bridging Reactome's Ontology with LLM Semantic Embeddings
abstract: Biological knowledgebases like Reactome provide high-quality pathways that include biological elements' relationships and textual descriptions (metadata). The quality of such pathways is granted by manual curation, that presents, however, significant scalability challenges. Lately, numerous NLP tools have been proposed to cope with this issue, leveraging textual information to automatically expand biological knowledgebases. However, little exploration has been done so far to assess whether relationships among textual descriptions mirror higher order biological relationships. This study explores whether human-written descriptions in Reactome can be used to infer the experts' defined global hierarchical structure. To test this, we extracted from Reactome the Homo Sapiens hierarchy of pathways and their reactions (Reactome Hierarchy), and used textual metadata to reconstruct a Semantic Hierarchy, combining a sentence transformer model (SPECTER2) with a modified agglomerative nesting algorithm and a graph reconstruction algorithm. Quantitative (Laplacian Spectral Distance and Bootstrapping) and qualitative (global topological metrics) analyses confirm our hypothesis and indicate that the global hierarchical structure of pathways can be inferred by experts textual metadata.

title: Low-Altitude Fluid Antenna Network with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) integrate terrestrial and aerial platforms to provide ubiquitous communication, sensing, and localization services for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. However, dynamic air-ground and air-air channels, abrupt blockages, and heterogeneous interference hinder the realization of this goal. Nevertheless, fluid antenna (FA), a cutting-edge multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique, overcomes these challenges by reconfiguring antenna positions to unlock additional spatial degrees-of-freedom. In this paper, towards bringing low-altitude FA networks into reality, we study the fast and high-performance FA reconfiguration for low-altitude FA networks with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Specifically, we present an electromagnetic digital twin (EM-DT)-assisted MARL framework. To fill the sim-to-real gap, we introduce a two-stage transfer learning framework. Our case study shows that joint FA positions and beamforming optimization can enhance the system sum-rate by 118.5%, compared to the fixed position baseline. This gain comes from the dynamic millisecond timescale reconfiguration of FA arrays and the adaptive steering of beams toward aerial users with mobility.

title: Интеграция классификатора эмоций в архитектуру диалоговой системы для корректировки текстовых ответов
abstract: This article examines the task of adjusting chatbot responses based on the user's emotional state without fine-tuning the language model. An approach is proposed in which a separate multimodal model assesses the user's state via voice and speech; the resulting label is then combined with the query and fed into Sber's GigaChat-2 to control the tone of the generated output. Manual testing demonstrated that incorporating this information enables the bot to generate more personalized and empathetic responses. This method operates without additional training, significantly reducing the computational costs associated with adjusting the model's responses.

title: Dynamic Programming with Memoryless Agents
abstract: This paper introduces a new paradigm for solving complex sequential decision-making problems – Dynamic Programming with Memoryless Agents (DPMA). The core idea is that intricate problems can be decomposed into a multitude of independent agents, each employing a simplified dynamic programming algorithm. These agents operate autonomously, exploring the solution space in a distributed manner. Coordination among the agents, achieved through a carefully designed protocol, ensures convergence towards the globally optimal solution. This approach addresses the scalability limitations inherent in traditional dynamic programming methods by leveraging the inherent parallelism of decentralized computation. The proposed method offers a potentially more efficient and adaptable framework for tackling problems across diverse domains, particularly those with high dimensionality or complex state spaces. The key contributions of this work lie in the formulation of the agent interaction protocol and the simplified dynamic programming algorithm suitable for implementation by individual agents.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Anomaly Detection in Time-Series Data
abstract: Anomaly detection in time-series data presents a significant challenge across numerous domains, including finance, industrial monitoring, and healthcare. Traditional methods frequently struggle to adapt to evolving data patterns, relying heavily on predefined thresholds or manually engineered features. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming to address these limitations. We demonstrate how probabilistic programming languages, such as Stan and PyMC, can be employed to model time-series data as probabilistic distributions. By utilizing Bayesian inference, we can effectively identify anomalies – data points that deviate substantially from the learned probabilistic model. The core of our method lies in treating anomalies not as outliers but as observations from a different, yet related, probability distribution. This allows for a more nuanced understanding of the data and enables detection of anomalies that would be missed by traditional techniques. The key advantages of this approach include adaptability to dynamic environments, the ability to incorporate prior knowledge, and a principled method for quantifying uncertainty in anomaly detection. The results presented illustrate the effectiveness of this probabilistic approach in identifying anomalies within time-series data.

title: A Similarity-Enhanced Transformer-LSTM Framework with IPOA for Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: Accurate prediction of PV output is critical for optimizing its absorption potential and ensuring the safe, stable, and cost-effective operation of the power grid. Yet, due to the intermittent and stochastic nature of photovoltaic power generation, establishing a highly precise prediction model presents significant difficulties. In this study, a hybrid forecasting framework integrating WCSD, CEEMDAN-FE, IPOA, and Transformer-LSTM is developed to improve PV power forecasting accuracy. Firstly, a new training data sample generation method based on WCSD is developed for determining the historical days having similar meteorological conditions to the predicted day. Secondly, CEEMDAN is employed to decompose original output sequence into an ensemble of components with different amplitudes and frequencies, where they were recombined as new set including a handful of components with low-frequency variation characteristics based on FE index. Thirdly, the IPOA is proposed for the first time, which couples Gaussian mutation and enhanced circle chaotic mapping. Next, the prediction model for each component is formulated by aid of Transformer-LSTM algorithm, the optimal hyperparameter combination of which is determined by IPOA method. Finally, the predicted results are obtained as the sum of individual component predictions. The prediction performance of the designed model is tested and verified via experimental analysis located in Yunnan Province, China and the publicly available Australian DKASC dataset. The empirical findings demonstrate that, in contrast to alternative benchmark models, our developed hybrid prediction model consistently attains superior prediction accuracy.

title: From Online Hate Speech to Online Hostility: Understanding and managing hate speech across disciplines
abstract: This document reports the theoretical background informing analysis of online hostility for the project “Together Against Online Hate Speech”. The goal of this report is to provide an overview of how our thinking about “hate speech” has developed over time: how it is defined in different disciplines and how may it be managed? This overview serves to define and conceptualize online hostility for comparison across Germany, the Netherlands and Spain on Instagram, X and TikTok. Our review highlights the challenges in defining hate speech, while emphasizing a general consensus among various disciplines calling for the protection against hate speech, through a variety of approaches, and a shift towards subjective and contextual understandings of online hostility. The project “Together Against Online Hate Speech” consists of the following partners: Sharing Perspectives Foundation, Build Up, IchBinHier, FundiPau, and the University of Amsterdam. The project is funded by the European Union (CERV-2024-CHAR-LITI-SPEECH). Views and opinions expressed are however those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect thoseof the European Union.
